A report from the year itself.

117977.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Tennessee
117977.note: Lubavitch.com (11 Sept 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'When Chabad of Memphis opened in 1994, it found a close-knit Jewish community of 10,000'. Rabbi Levi and Rivka Klein (therebbesimpact.com: 1994).

118476.name: Chabad of Knoxville
118476.note: Podcast profile: Rabbi Yossi and Miriam Esther Wilhelm 'moved to Knoxville, TN in 2001'. therebbesimpact.com: 2001.

211894.name: Chabad of Nashville
211894.note: Its own site: 'established in 1999' (Rabbi Yitzchok and Esther Tiechtel). Long before, the Frierdiker Rebbe had sent Rabbi Zalman Posner to Nashville (1949), who started the Akiva day school; not a Chabad house. Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 142 Belle Forest Circle, Nashville (May 2010); it is now at 95 Bellevue Road, Nashville, listed there by Nov 2020, so it moved there between May 2010 and Nov 2020.

earlier.where: 142 Belle Forest Circle, Nashville (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived May 13 2010)

384002.name: Stanford Eisenberg Knoxville Jewish Day School
384002.note: Knox News (via CrownHeights.info, 19 Oct 2006): 'The school, which opened in August, currently serves a combined kindergarten and first-grade class'; Miriam Esther Wilhelm its head. Named for the father of a donor (seed money $150,000).

582611.name: Rohr Chabad House at Vanderbilt
582611.note: Lubavitch.com (24 Oct 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'Chabad Opens Student Center At Vanderbilt University', Rabbi Shlomo and Nechama Rothstein its new representatives (comments: 'finally its official', 'we can't wait for you to come'). The Jewish Observer (Dec 2024): they began 17 years ago. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 436 Village at Vanderbilt, Nashville; it is now at 111 23rd Ave North, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 436 Village at Vanderbilt, Nashville (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

957897.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Chattanooga
957897.note: Chabad.org / CrownHeights.info: Rabbi Shaul and Rosie Perlstein arrived in Chattanooga from Brooklyn in 2009 and have co-directed the Chabad Jewish Center since then; first on Pisgah Ave., later a former Masonic Lodge (2015).

earlier.where: Pisgah Ave.

6549164.name: Chabad of Williamson County
6549164.note: The Jewish Observer (Nashville), Oct 2024: 'New Chabad center opens in Williamson County' (Cool Springs), Rabbi Mendel and Chana Baron, the county's first Chabad house. chabad.org's listing number (6549164) is from late 2024 too.

117623.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Louisiana
117623.note: Its own history page: 'In November of 1975' the Rebbe sent Rabbi Zelig and Bluma Rivkin to New Orleans (a Chabad.org obituary's 1973 is an outlier; therebbesimpact.com also has 1973). Chabad House Uptown near Tulane from 1975-76; Metairie branch 1990; Southern Mississippi Aug 2014; Baton Rouge Aug 2015.

174119.name: Tulane Chabad
174119.note: The Uptown Chabad House by Tulane: Rabbi Zelig Rivkin recalls they 'opened the Chabad House on Purim of 1976' after renovating it (the Jewish Women's Archive also has 1976). Chabad of Louisiana's own page says it began working out of it in fall 1975.

3517860.name: Undergraduate Program at Tulane University
3517860.note: Tulane News, Sept 2015: Rabbi Leibel and Mushka Lipskier 'have taken over undergraduate programming at the Rohr Chabad Jewish Student Center at Tulane University'; the Rivkins moved to graduate students.

119695.name: Slater Torah Academy
119695.note: Chabad's day school (Torah Academy, renamed for Joseph and Rosina Slater in 2018). A Times of Israel blog: founded in 1993; the Tulane biography of Bluma Rivkin: it grew out of the Lakeshore Hebrew Day School and opened in 1994; Wikipedia: in its permanent facility from 1994. therebbesimpact.com: 1993. Destroyed by Katrina, reopened Jan 2006. Checked (Nov 7): NOLA.com, Sept 9 2018 ('Torah Academy celebrates renaissance ...'): 'The school initially started in 1970 as Lakeshore Hebrew Day School. In 1994, it became the Torah Academy'. With the Tulane biography and Wikipedia also giving 1994, the year is 1994 (was 1993 from one blog), high.

536224.name: Camp Gan Israel
536224.note: No start year found (Rabbi Zalman Groner). chabad.org's listing number (536224) is from about 2007, so it ran by then. Its chabad.org listing went up on Jul 3 2007 (chabad.org's own record), so it existed by then.

117622.name: Chabad Center of Metairie
117622.note: Rabbi Yossie Nemes (Jewish Women's Archive oral history): 'We moved here in August of 1990'; Chabad of Louisiana: 'In 1990, Chabad of Louisiana opened a branch in Metairie'.

2637896.name: Congregation Beth Israel
2637896.note: Chabad of Louisiana: 'In August of 2014 Chabad of Southern Mississippi was founded in Biloxi serving the Gulf Coast region' (Rabbi Akiva and Hannah Hall). The listing is the Gulfport congregation Beth Israel, which is older; the year is when Chabad began serving it. Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 1648 Wiltshire Boulevard, Biloxi (Oct 2014, Jan 2016); then 2030 Pass Road, Biloxi (Oct 2019); it is now at 12277 Three Rivers Road, Gulfport (Congregation Beth Israel), so it moved there after Oct 2019 (when, not found). Until at least 2019 the listing was Chabad of South(ern) Mississippi in Biloxi; it now carries Congregation Beth Israel's name and address.

earlier.where: 1648 Wiltshire Boulevard, Biloxi (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Oct 9 2014 to Jan 4 2016)
2030 Pass Road, Biloxi (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Oct 23 2019)

2819121.name: Chabad of Baton Rouge
2819121.note: Chabad of Louisiana: Chabad of Baton Rouge opened in August (summer) 2015, for the Baton Rouge community and LSU students; Rabbi Peretz and Chaya Mushka Kazen founded the city's first permanent Chabad House (Chabad.org).

117723.name: Merkos - Chabad of Rhode Island / Chabad of Providence
117723.note: ChabadInfo: Rabbi Yehoshua and Mishla Laufer 'established the Providence-based Chabad Center of greater Rhode Island in 1979'. 360-362 Hope Street.

7222988.name: Chabad of Providence
7222988.note: No source found (Rabbi Berel Laufer). chabad.org's listing number (7222988) is from about early 2026 (between late 2025's 7117900 and mid-2026's 7309271). Perhaps a new branch of his family's Providence center (1979). Its chabad.org listing went up on Apr 13 2026 (chabad.org's own record), so it existed by then.

117949.name: Chabad of West Bay Chai Center
117949.note: Its IRS record (Chabad of West Bay Chai Center Inc, Warwick) dates from 1995. Jewish Rhode Island: 'in 1998, Laufer moved back home ... and became the rabbi at the Chabad of West Bay Chai Center', so it existed by 1998.

118593.name: Chabad of College Hill
118593.note: No founding report found. Its nonprofit record dates from 2003; its listing number (118593) is from chabad.org's first directory (about 2003). Brown's Chabad House, 12 Olive St., for Brown, RISD and Johnson & Wales; Rabbi Mendel and Chana Laufer. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Chabad at Brown on Instagram (post of Aug 26 2025, dated by its post ID; https://www.instagram.com/p/DN1NbXF3oNQ/): 'we are back at 12 Olive Street! Open House tomorrow', after renovations (the Brown Daily Herald, Nov 2025, mentions the renovated Chabad of College Hill); it was at 12 Olive Street in lubavitch.com's directory in Sept 2011, and its chabad.org listing gives 14 Olive Street.

419786.name: Chabad House of Barrington-Newport
419786.note: Warren Times Gazette (via CrownHeights.info, 15 Nov 2006): Rabbi Moshe and Mirel Laufer moved to Barrington 'in May' (2006) to serve the East Bay.

2743772.name: Chabad House of Northern Rhode Island
2743772.note: The Jewish Voice (June 2016): Rabbi Aryeh and Mushka Laufer 'have recently established the Chabad House of northern R.I.'; 'This past September' (2015), before their official move from Providence to Lincoln, they ran High Holy Day services in Smithfield. Settled in Lincoln at the end of 2015. Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 7 Wake Robin Road #1402, Lincoln (Dec 2015); it is now at 1767 Old Louisquisset Pike, Lincoln, listed there by Dec 2019, so it moved there between Dec 2015 and Dec 2019.

earlier.where: 7 Wake Robin Road #1402, Lincoln (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Dec 19 2015)

3329974.name: Chabad of the University of Rhode Island
3329974.note: Chabad.org News, Oct 31 2017 ('Doubling Presence in a Decade, 14 New Chabad Campus Centers Opened This Year'): 'Rabbi Avraham Adam ("Avi") and Tzippy Goldstein arrived at the University of Rhode Island in Kingston, R.I., last year before Sukkot', i.e. before Sukkot 2016 (the listing number also points to 2016). Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 100 Fortin Road, Unit 4, Kingston (Nov 2019); it is now at 26 Lower College Road, Kingston, so it moved there after Nov 2019 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 100 Fortin Road, Unit 4, Kingston (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Nov 13 2019)

5097669.name: Chabad of South County
5097669.note: Its own page ('The Reinitzes'): 'In August 2021, Rabbi Mendy and Lieba Reinitz and their daughter Mushky arrived in South Kingstown, RI to open a Chabad center for the Jewish population of Southern RI.' Its chabad.org listing went up June 2 2021, just before; therebbesimpact.com also has 2021. At 77 Main St., South Kingstown.

117736.name: Chabad of Vermont
117736.note: Chabad.org (20 Dec 2018): 'In the winter of 1983' Rabbi Yitzchok and Zeesy Raskin were appointed by the Rebbe 'as the new Chabad-Lubavitch emissaries to Vermont'; one of their first acts was a menorah at City Hall. A Chabad article also says they opened the center in 1983, but the Brattleboro Reformer (2012) and Front Porch Forum say 1984. Rabbi Eliyahu and Draizy Junik, now its directors, came in 2014. Checked (Nov 7): its own site (https://www.chabadvt.org/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/447745/jewish/About-Chabad-of-Burlington.htm): 'Founded by Rabbi Yitzchok and Zeesy Raskin in 1984'; so appointed in the winter of 1983 and founded 1984 — the year taken is the center's own (was 1983), medium as the two are a year apart.

119676.name: Mikvah Chaya Mushka
119676.note: No year found. The Chabad mikvah at 221 Summit Street, supervised by Chabad of Vermont; its listing number (119676) is from chabad.org's first directory (about 2003), so it existed by then. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

389837.name: Chabad @ UVM
389837.note: Lubavitch.com: Chabad at UVM opened in 2006 under Rabbi Zalman and Chani Wilhelm, first in a small apartment, later a three-story house near student housing.

1671455.name: Chabad of Southern Vermont
1671455.note: Chabad.org (31 July 2012): Rabbi Avremy and Chaya Raskin moved from Brooklyn to Brattleboro 'earlier this month' to open a Chabad center; the Brattleboro Reformer (Sept 2012): they arrived 'in early July'. (therebbesimpact.com gives the couple 2011.) Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 275 Western Avenue, Brattleboro (Jan 2013); then 59 Country Hill, Brattleboro (Oct 2016, Dec 2019); it is now at 1130 Upper Dummerston Road, Brattleboro, so it moved there after Dec 2019 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 275 Western Avenue, Brattleboro (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Jan 24 2013)
59 Country Hill, Brattleboro (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Oct 23 2016 to Dec 8 2019)

2698131.name: Chabad of Bennington County
2698131.note: Chabad.org's 'Chabad House of the Week' post (Facebook and Instagram, June 15 2026 by the post's ID, https://www.instagram.com/p/DZnNE7ek_i9/; read from the search index, as Facebook is not scraped): 'Chabad of Manchester has been led by Rabbi Menachem and Faygie Andrusier since the summer of 2015.' Its own About page, first published July 23 2015 (https://www.manchesterjewishlife.com/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/3015631/jewish/About-Us.htm), agrees: they 'are living in Manchester, VT with their 8 children and are excited to make Manchester their home ... Please check our website for more information and launch dates'. Medium, because its chabad.org listing already went up on Nov 3 2014 (therebbesimpact.com also has 2014), before the move. Now at 171 Sargent Lane, Manchester. Archived copies of its chabad.org listing (Wayback Machine) show it at 86 Two Cow Lane, Manchester Center (Aug 2017); it is now at 171 Sargent Lane, Manchester, listed there by Dec 2019, so it moved there between Aug 2017 and Dec 2019.

earlier.where: 86 Two Cow Lane, Manchester Center (its address on its chabad.org listing as archived Aug 16 2017)

3548886.name: Middlebury Chabad
3548886.note: Chabad.org News, Oct 31 2017 ('14 New Chabad Campus Centers Opened This Year'): 'Rabbi Binyamin (aka "Rabbi B") and Davida Murray, co-directors of Middlebury Chabad in Middlebury, Vt., arrived this August'. (therebbesimpact.com: 2017.)

5644326.name: Chabad of Northwest Vermont
5644326.note: JNS, Nov 21 2022 ('A new Chabad every three days', on the 120 new Chabad centers of the past year): 'two new Chabad centers have opened in Vermont: Chabad of Northwest Vermont in South Burlington, led by Rabbi Shmuel and Gittel Grossman, and Chabad of Stowe'. (therebbesimpact.com and the listing number also point to 2022.)

5684614.name: Chabad of Stowe
5684614.note: Waterbury Roundabout (Dec 2022): Rabbi Boruch and Sara Simon 'recently moved to Waterbury Center' from Miami as Chabad emissaries to the Stowe area; on Merkos's list of new shluchim grants (COLlive).

117609.name: Lubavitch of Iowa
117609.note: Chabad.org: 'Since 1992, when Rabbi Yossi and Chanie Jacobson first established Lubavitch of Iowa in Des Moines'; the Jewish Virtual Library also has 1992.

602103.name: Talmud Torah
602103.note: No year found. A Hebrew school of Lubavitch of Iowa (1992). Its chabad.org listing went up on Nov 27 2007 (chabad.org's own record), so it existed by then.

7465212.name: YJP Des Moines
7465212.note: Its own About page (Aug 2026): 'Young Jewish Professionals Des Moines was established in 2026'; 'Rabbi Moshe & Chaya Vorovitch together with their daughter Basya moved to and founded Young Jewish Professionals Des Moines in 2026.' Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

7465215.name: Cteen Iowa
7465215.note: Rabbi Moshe Zalman Vorovitch's CTeen Iowa, its chabad.org listing made together with YJP Des Moines's (7465212), which the Vorovitchs founded on moving to Des Moines in 2026; CTeen's own start isn't stated.

118520.name: Lubavitch of Iowa City
118520.note: Its own site: 'Chabad UIowa is an independent 501(c)3 nonprofit organization, founded in 2001.' (Rabbi Avrohom and Chaya Blesofsky; therebbesimpact.com: 2002.) Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

118635.name: Chabad of North East Iowa

Checked (Nov 7): its own About page (Mar 2023, https://www.chabadneiowa.com/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/5875604/jewish/About-Us.htm): 'Rabbi Aron & Yehudis Schimmel established Chabad N.E. Iowa in 1997.' The year is the center's own (was 1998 from COLlive's rough count), so high.

3209374.name: Cheder Menachem Boys School/Beis Chaya Mushka Girls School

Founded 1994, 1-8' and 'Oholei Menachem Cheder, 300 Hill St ... Postville, IA ... Founded 1994, 1-8'. A directory's year, so medium. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

3209388.name: Mesivta Lubavitch Beth Shalom Postville
3209388.note: Its own site: 'The Mesivta of Postville was founded in 1997 by R' Sholom Mordechai Halevi ben Rivkah Rubashkin and his family', who funded it for its first twelve years.

3697415.name: Lubavitch of Ames
3697415.note: The Greater Des Moines Jewish Press, Winter Edition (December 2017 to February 2018), 'What is Chabad-Lubavitch': 'Rabbi Leibel and Malka Jacobson have moved to Ames to establish a Chabad center' and 'the Jacobson's just moved and have barely had time to settle in'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 4 2017; L'Chaim weekly no. 1501 (Miketz 5778, Dec 2017) also reports the move. Serves Iowa State University; 414 Stanton Ave.

117690.name: National Committee for Jewish Education

1676572.name: Heichal Menachem of Monsey
1676572.note: Monsey (no shetach). Chabadpedia: founded on 19 Kislev 5759 (8 Dec 1998) by Rabbi Gedalia Oberlander; Anash.org also has 5759. Its lending library opened in 5775 (2014-15); his son Rabbi Dovid Oberlander has run it since 2012.

4166847.name: Mesivta Lev Tmimim
4166847.note: COLlive, Apr 25 2015 ('Second Mesivta Opens in Monsey'): 'A new Mesivta named Lev Tmimim is being opened by Rabbi Gil Hami' for the coming school year (2015-16); Rabbi Hami is 'its founder and director'. Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

4173591.name: Mesivta Lubavitch of Monsey
4173591.note: Monsey (no shetach). CrownHeights.info, 22 Sept 2014: 'a new Mesivta opened this year in Monsey'; it 'opened its doors on Zayin Elul' (7 Elul 5774, 2 Sept 2014) to the students of Shiur Alef.

6656482.name: Cheder Zichron Shmuel
6656482.note: Anash.org, Feb 28 2023 ('High-Level Chinuch That Doesn't Compromise Any Student'): 'The high-level, Yiddish-immersion moisad opened its doors last year with only two classes comprising a total of eleven boys' (Cheder Zichron Shmuel, Rockland County; Rabbi Moshe Gourarie, founder and dean). Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page.

7109019.name: Mayan Torah Tomchei Tmimim
7109019.note: COLlive, Aug 27 2023 ('Mesivta of Pomona Expands With New Location, Staff'): 'Yeshiva Mayan Torah of Pomona NY, opened for its second year in a larger facility' ('founded on ... the Rebbe Rashab's vision for Tomchei Tmimim'; menahel Rabbi Nochum Labkowski; started by Rabbi Yoseph and Tzippy Vigler), so it opened in 2022. 285958.name: Camp Gan Israel

119209.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Ottawa
119209.note: Torah Day School's profile: 'Rabbi Hayes moved to Ottawa in 1977 together with his wife Chana and newborn daughter, as an emissary of Chabad Lubavitch'; he helped open a preschool, afternoon school, day camp and day school. therebbesimpact.com: the couple 1977, the center 1978.

118369.name: Jewish Youth Library of Ottawa
118369.note: Founded by Devora and Dr. Yosef Caytak in 1983, in their basement (Lubavitch.com, 'A Jewish Youth Library Grows and Grows'); its own building from 1989, then a preschool and summer camp. COLlive, 11 May 2014: its 30th anniversary dinner, 4 May 2014.

Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

118251.name: Ottawa Torah Centre Chabad
118251.note: Founded in Barrhaven in 1997 by Rabbi Menachem Mendel and Dina Blum, in their basement, then a leased store (Ottawa Jewish Bulletin; Choose Ottawa); its building at 111 Lamplighters Drive, Ottawa's first new synagogue in about 30 years, opened 2014. therebbesimpact.com: 1998.

a leased store

118589.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Centrepointe was established by Rabbi Chaim and Bassy Mendelsohn - right before the High Holidays of 2002'; Rabbi Mendelsohn's LinkedIn: Chabad of Centrepointe, Sep 2002 - present. (therebbesimpact.com: 2002.)

559424.name: Chabad of Kanata
559424.note: Ottawa Jewish Bulletin (about 2021, 'Russian-speaking Jews more engaged with community thanks to Genesis grant'): 'Gershzon said in 2005, the "Acheinu Board" was established to address the growing needs of a Russian-speaking Jewish population, which eventually led to the development of the Chabad of Kanata by bringing Rabbi Gershzon to Ottawa', so after 2005 (https://www.ottawajewishbulletin.com/jewish-ottawa/russian-speaking-jews-more-engaged-with-community-thanks-to-genesis-grant). The Chesed Fund (undated): the Gershzons 'founded Chabad of Kanata almost two decades ago'. therebbesimpact.com and the listing number point to 2007 (leads). Its chabad.org listing went up on Sep 16 2007 (chabad.org's own record), so it existed by then. It began as the Jewish Russian Community Centre of Ottawa (JRCC Ottawa): its site, archived June 16 2008 (copyright 2007), names Rabbi Michoel Gershzon, regional director, and Mrs. Miriam Gershzon (https://web.archive.org/web/20080616173605/http://www.jrccottawa.org/), and lubavitch.com's directory as archived Aug 30 2011 lists the Jewish Russian Community Center of Ottawa at 15 Hansen Ave. (Kanata). 5456142.name: Chabad of Wellington West
5456142.note: 'Chabad of Wellington West was founded in 2022 by Ottawa-born Rabbi Moshe Caytak and his wife, Sheina' (The CJN); a 'New Shluchim to Wellington' notice (CrownHeights.info); a fourth-anniversary celebration in 2026. Now at 166 Huron Avenue.

4406734.name: Chabad of Westboro Village

7475377.name: Irving Aaron Kitchen of Kindness

117602.note: Sarasota Herald-Tribune (via CrownHeights.info, 26 Dec 2005): 'Shortly after moving here from California in 1990, Steinmetz...'. CrownHeights.info, 28 Feb 2006 (its 11th annual dinner): Chabad's headquarters was 'the small guest room in Rabbi Steinmetz' apartment' when he 'first arrived to the city 15 years ago'.

117889.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Northeast Florida
117889.note: Chabad.org, 16 Nov 2010: Rabbi Yoseph and Rivkie Kahanov 'have lived in Jacksonville for 18 years' (so 1992); Anash later: they 'built and served the greater Jacksonville community for over 30 years'. A 2011 blog calls him its founder. The Mandarin center (an acre and a half) more than doubled in 2010.

117592.name: Lubavitch Hebrew Academy
117592.note: COLlive, 4 Sept 2024: Rabbi Yossie Denburg, 'the founder and dean of LHA': 'As we begin our 40th year of service ... the Rebbe's Bracha to my wife and I in 5745, for Hatzlacha for Chinuch in Broward County' (a 40th year in 2024-25 gives a first year of 1985-86). School listings: founded in 1985. (Earlier called the Hebrew Academy Community School.)

559661.name: South Florida Jewish Academy
559661.note: Chabad.org (via CrownHeights.info, 27 Aug 2007): the new South Florida Jewish Academy for children with special needs began classes on Monday, Aug. 20 (2007), with 15 children, in the building of the former South Florida Academy of Learning, which Chabad of Coconut Creek & West Pompano Beach bought in April with the Tabacinic family's help.

117601.name: Chabad Chayil - Highland Lakes Jewish Center
117601.note: Founded 'in the late 1980s' by Rabbi Dovid Bryn (South Florida Sun Times; the Jewish Press: 'the local Chabad center in the 1980's'); after his death in 2002 Rabbi Moishe and Layah Kievman have led it (Chabad.org, Jan 2022). Exact year not found yet.

117948.name: Hollywood Community Synagogue - Chabad
117948.note: COLlive, 3 July 2015: after the eviction on Tisha B'Av 5774 (Aug 2014), Rabbi Joseph Korf said the restart 'was 1990 all over again', i.e. as when they began; the center was reclaimed on 12 Tammuz 5775 (June 2015). The Sun-Sentinel had it moving out of its house at 2215 N. 46th Ave. therebbesimpact.com: the center and Joseph & Elisheva Korf 1990. Only indirect: to check.

117960.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Southwest Broward
117960.note: COLlive, 18 July 2022: 'After a unique and life changing blessing from the Rebbe 31 years ago, Rabbi Pinny and Gitty moved to Florida to be trailblazing shluchim, opening Chabad of Southwest Broward (SWB) in Cooper City', 'operating out of a small modest modular trailer for 30 years' (so 1992). IRS: 'Chabad Lubavitch Of Southwest Broward Inc', exempt from Dec 1993 (ProPublica). therebbesimpact.com: the couple 1992, the center 1993.

earlier.where: a small modular trailer, Cooper City

117969.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Daytona
117969.note: Its own site: established in 1993; COLlive: Rabbi Pinchas Ezagui 'has been in Daytona since 1993'; news of 2008-10 ('15 years', '17 years') agree.

117991.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Boynton Beach
117991.note: Its own pages: Rabbi Sholom and Dinie Ciment 'arrive in Boynton in 1994'; its mission statement: founded 1994 with a handful of members. (Sun-Sentinel, May 2008: small 'thirteen years ago'.)

118196.name: Chabad Jewish Center of the Florida Keys
118196.note: Chabad.org, 22 Feb 2010 ('Florida Jews Mark Half a Century of Chabad Activities'): Rabbi Yaakov Zucker 'arrived as a newlywed in 1995, sent there by the Korfs', and directs the Chabad Jewish Center of the Florida Keys and Key West.

118198.name: Chabad of Weston Center for Jewish Life
118198.note: Our City Weston (Feb 2023): Chabad of Weston 'has been serving the local Jewish community since it first opened in 1996' (Rabbi Yisroel and Leah Spalter). Its new 16,000 sq ft center was built while it ran from a trailer for two years (Lubavitch.com).

118284.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Martin & S. Lucie County
118284.note: 10 Sept 2018: Rabbi Shlomo and Daniella Uminer's Chabad center, 'which they founded when they moved here from Brooklyn 23 years ago' (so 1995); Lubavitch.com, separately: they have led the community for 23 years. IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Martin-St Lucie County Inc', exempt from Feb 2001. (therebbesimpact.com: 1999.) A 2.5-acre campus on Sunset Trail, Palm City.

118287.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Sunny Isles Beach
118287.note: Its CYP page: 'Our synagogue began as Sunny Isles Chabad in 1994 even before Sunny Isles Beach was incorporated or named as a city', in 'a small office space on the second floor of the RK Plaza at 170th Street'; 'Various moves followed until eventually, the congregation moved to the ground floor of the King David in 2004.' Confirmed by the IRS record: 'Chabad Center Of Sunny Isles Inc', exempt from Aug 1994 (ProPublica). Rabbi Yisrael and Toby Baron.

earlier.where: an office on the second floor of RK Plaza, 170th Street
the ground floor of the King David

118356.name: Chabad Lubavitch of the Panhandle - Tallahassee
118356.note: Chabad-Lubavitch of the Panhandle 'was established in 2000' by Rabbi Schneur Zalman and Chanie Oirechman, for FSU students and Tallahassee (news of the May 2022 fire that destroyed its building; Lubavitch.com). Panama City Beach, Destin and Pensacola grew from it.

118367.name: Chabad of East Boca Raton
118367.note: Boca Raton Tribune (May 2010, its 10th anniversary): Chabad of Boca Raton appointed Rabbi Ruvi and Ahuva New to open an East Boca branch in September 1999; it began in their living room, then a storefront on Palmetto Park Road, then from 2002 a larger rented facility; a site at 770 East Palmetto Park Road was gifted by Irving and Judy Litwak.

earlier.where: Rabbi Ruvi and Ahuva New's living room
a storefront on Palmetto Park Road
a larger rented facility

118379.name: Lubavitch Chabad Jewish Student Center
118379.note: Chabad.org: Rabbi Berl and Chanie Goldman have seen Jewish life at UF grow 'since they first arrived in 2000'; a 2010 report: 'ten years after moving to Gainesville to establish a student Jewish center'. Early on it ran from tents, trailers and temporary buildings; the 23,000 sq ft Tabacinic center at 2021 NW Fifth Ave. came later.

118475.name: Chabad of Coral Springs
118475.note: Anash ('Chabad of Coral Springs celebrates 36 years and counting'): 'Established in 1986, Chabad of Coral Springs began when Rabbi Yossi Denburg and his wife Rivka were sent to South Florida' to build a Hebrew day school and a Chabad House; Rabbi Avraham Friedman became executive director in 1991. (Coral Springs Talk counted its 36th anniversary in 2023, and therebbesimpact.com says 1987: a year later.)

118411.name: Chabad Key Biscayne Jewish Center
118411.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 Nov 2002: 'three years ago, Rabbi Yoel and Rivka Caroline began introducing various Jewish activities' on Key Biscayne (so 1999); Chabad of Key Biscayne 'moved into a home of its own just in time Rosh Hashana 5763' (Sept 2002) at 211 Greenwood Drive. IRS: 'Chabad Of Key Biscayne Inc', exempt from May 2002. Now 101 Harbor Drive (Rabbi Avremel Caroline).

earlier.where: 211 Greenwood Drive, Key Biscayne

118437.name: Chabad of South Orlando
118437.note: Heritage Florida Jewish News, 3 Apr 2015: 'After having a presence in the southwest Orlando area for 15 years' (so 2000); Chabad.org, separately: 'the 2000 arrival of Rabbi Yosef and Chani Konikov'. (Chabad of Greater Orlando's history has them hired in 1998; a 2016 Heritage piece says 1999; an Anash account says activities began in 2001 from their rented home.) Earlier on Tamarind Circle; the Center of Jewish Life at 7347 Sand Lake Road from about 2015.

earlier.where: Tamarind Circle, Orlando

118514.name: Downtown Jewish Center Chabad
118514.note: Its own home page has both: 'DJCC has been serving the Fort Lauderdale community since 2000' and 'Rabbi Schneur & Devorah Kaplan, emissaries of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, founded the Downtown Jewish Center Chabad in 2003.' Directory listings (Las Olas Boulevard association; MapQuest) also say 2000. The earlier year is used; the two disagree, so medium. (VIN News, 2009: then not on chabad.org's list.) 900 E Broward Blvd.

118594.name: Chabad Russian Center of S. Florida
118594.note: Miami Herald (via CrownHeights.info, 17 Dec 2007): Rabbi Alexander Kaller 'came into town in 2002'; the synagogue 'humbly started off in 2002' in the rabbi's living room, moved after a few months to the meeting room at the Oceania condos, then to a 65-seat storefront synagogue in a strip mall; its waterfront center opened in 2026.

earlier.where: Rabbi Alexander Kaller's living room
the meeting room at the Oceania condos
a storefront synagogue in a strip mall, Sunny Isles Beach

118653.name: Chabad at the Beaches

118646.name: Chabad of Naples
118646.note: Jewish Federation of Greater Naples' Connections 2022: established by Rabbi Fishel and Ettie Zaklos in 2004 (also 'Since 2004' on a kosher directory). 1789 Mandarin Road. therebbesimpact.com: 2003.

118534.name: Chabad @ University of Miami

Nothing found shows it ran without a break until 2001, so the year is the Felligs' opening and 1973 is kept under 'earlier'. (Was 1973, medium, before Nov 6.)

118656.name: Chabad at Midtown Miami

Now at 221 NE 29th St.; COLlive (6 Nov 2026): their son Rabbi Mendel Gopin joined 'Chabad at Midtown, which his father founded and leads'.

118658.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Jupiter

119832.name: Chabad Ocean Synagogue
119832.note: Lubavitch.com (obituary of Chasiah Kudan): she and Rabbi Dovid Kudan moved to South Broward in 1989 to run youth programs for Chabad of South Broward; 'The next year' they opened the Chabad Ocean Synagogue. earlier.where: the Hilton, Hollywood
Sea Air Towers
Hallmark Condominiums

118660.name: California Club Chabad

(A tribute calls the late Rabbi Dovid Bryn, d. 2002, founder of 'the California Club Shul' too: an earlier minyan there, perhaps.)

earlier.where: a mall, California Club area

160742.name: Chabad of Brandon & South Shore
160742.note: Rabbi Mendel and Tzippy Rubashkin opened Chabad of Brandon 'in the summer of 2004'; a 2005 article: he 'started Chabad of Brandon a year ago' after moving from Brooklyn. Later its Jewish Discovery Center (Valrico, 2014).

169223.name: Chabad at Florida International University

10031 SW 15 Terrace

rented space at schools and office buildings

223658.name: Chabad of Cape Coral

212291.name: Chabad of Bonita Springs, Estero & FGCU

an office suite in a strip mall off Old 41 Road (Bernwood Centre), Bonita Springs

118571.name: Chabad Jewish Center

Chabad.org, 5 April 2011 ('Larry King Entertains Florida Crowd'): Dr. Richard Sorkin 'moved to the area about eight years ago, around the same time as Alter and Chaya Korf', which agrees (2003). Later at 533 4th Street North (land bought 2019, groundbreaking April 2023).

a leased storefront, 6151 Central Ave.

257624.name: Chabad of Venice & North Port

Herald-Tribune (CrownHeights.info, March 2016): 'started ... with a handful of people in their living room in 2005'; land for the campus bought 2012.

earlier.where: the Schmerlings' home, North Port

384721.name: Chabad of Palm Beach Gardens
384721.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of Palm Beach Gardens was founded on April 30, 2006'. earlier.where: the Viglers' living room
Timber Trace Elementary School (services), then Downtown at the Gardens and Loehmann's Plaza

325854.name: Chabad of Pembroke Pines
325854.note: Sun-Sentinel (CrownHeights.info, 6 Oct 2011): 'Andrusier, who's originally from Brooklyn, NY, founded the synagogue in 2005'; in 2011 it was still 'moving from a rented location to a more permanent place'.

371894.name: Chabad of West Pasco

As attendance grew, they rented space in the Trinity Oaks' shopping center; a permanent home in 2013-14. Chabad.org (July 2013): they 'moved to the area more than seven years ago'; co-directors 'since 2006'. A grand opening at 9945 Trinity Blvd. was in 2009.

earlier.where: a rented three-bedroom house in Trinity (home and synagogue)
Trinity Oaks shopping center, 9945 Trinity Blvd.

347029.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Doral
347029.note: Miami Herald (CrownHeights.info, 16 Oct 2006, at Sukkot): 'Since their arrival in Doral a year ago, the Brashevitzky family has welcomed ... worshipers for weekly Chabad services held at their home, 5353 NW 109th Ct.'; 'One year ago, he established the Chabad Jewish Center in Doral' (fall 2005). IRS: 'Chabad Jewish Center Of Doral Inc', exempt from June 2006. (Later counts are a year short: Miami Herald, May 2009, 'three years later'; Doral Family Journal, 23 March 2013, 'established seven years ago'.) earlier.where: the Brashevitzkys' home, 5353 NW 109th Ct.
a shopping center, 9725 NW 41st St.

334256.name: Chabad of Southside

Rabbi Shmuel (Shmuli) and Chana Novack; early on in rented meeting rooms and libraries; the 12,000 sq ft center opened in 2019.

312032.name: Chabad of Charlotte County

'After growing out of the in-home Chabad House, the Jacobsons began renting a storefront, where they held services and activities for nine years before purchasing the new 9,500 square foot building', moved in just before Rosh Hashanah 2022: 'the community's third Chabad House building'.

a rented storefront

298937.name: Lubavitch Aventura South

Miami Herald (CrownHeights.info, 17 Nov 2011): Lubavitch Aventura South had rented two salons at the Aventura Courtyard Marriott; its first place of its own, a temporary sanctuary of five trailers, opened five days before Rosh Hashanah 2011.

earlier.where: rented rooms at the Aventura Courtyard Marriott

269188.name: Chabad of Deerfield Beach

Start year not found yet; lead: therebbesimpact.com 2004.

118666.name: Chabad of West Palm Beach
118666.note: Lubavitch.com 'New Appointments' (25 Aug 2004): 'West Palm Beach, Florida: Rabbi and Mrs. Mendy Kornfeld.' The chabad.org listing (118666) and therebbesimpact.com also point to 2004. 118350.name: Chabad House in Miami Beach and Chabad House on Wheels
118350.note: Miami Herald (COLlive, 24 July 2011): 'Katz's RV ministry, Chabad on Wheels, started 12 years ago, when he was completing rabbinical school in New York' (count back: 1999); 'Katz has opened a bricks-and-mortar synagogue on Lincoln Lane'. IRS: 'Chabad House On Wheels', Rabbi Zev Katz, ruling June 2002.

290969.name: Chabad of N.E. Hollywood & Dania
290969.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of N.E. Now also Chabad of East Hollywood / Shul of the Lakes, 1350 Harrison Street. Existed by 2005 (earlier bound), which agrees.

earlier.where: Hollywood Women's Club, 501 N. 14th Ave.

1335573.name: Chabad of Clay County
1335573.note: First Coast Chabad blog (8 March 2011) announced the new Clay County center, the first Jewish institution of any kind in the county, with Rabbi Shmuly and Shaina Feldman. Clay Today (CrownHeights.info, 22 June 2011): 'Since the Feldmans moved to Fleming Island in April they have hosted several events'.

1241523.name: Chabad of Clearwater

Rabbi Levi and Miriam Hodakov had been program directors at Chabad of Pinellas (Palm Harbor) since 2006. Then the Tabacinic Chabad Center (2014) and the former Bank of America on Belleair Road (2023).

the Tabacinic Chabad Center

1274159.name: Chabad Jewish Center of West Boynton and West Lake Worth

COLlive, 2 June 2013 (Greater Boynton's 18th gala): 'A new satellite Boynton Chabad center has opened, directed by Rabbi & Mrs. Yosef Raichik, in the western part of the city.'

1269573.name: Las Olas Chabad Jewish Center
1269573.note: Chabad.org (22 Nov 2011): 'Last December, Rabbi Chaim and Chaya Mushka Slavaticki moved to Fort Lauderdale, Fla., to open a new Chabad-Lubavitch center'; they were 'getting ready to open the doors to a rented storefront they're calling the Chabad Jewish Center of Fort Lauderdale Beach'. 2480687.name: Chabad of the Emerald Coast
2480687.note: Destin Log (CrownHeights.info, 13 Oct 2013): 'Chabad-Lubavitch recently opened a new branch on Florida's Emerald Coast. 427844.name: Chabad of Lake Worth
427844.note: Shmais.com (CrownHeights.info, 5 July 2006): 'Rabbi and Mrs. Mendy and Leah Rosenfeld of New Haven CT will IYH be moving on Shlichus to East Lake Worth, Florida where they will establish Chabad of Green Acres and Atlantis.' IRS: 'Chabad Of East Lake Worth Greenacres And Atlantis Inc' (care of Menachem M Rosenfeld), exempt from Feb 2008.

300767.name: Chabad of NW Coral Springs (the Chai Center)
300767.note: Its own About page: 'Established in 2005, The Chai Center Chabad is directed by Rabbi Hershy Bronstein and his wife Chanie' (an independent affiliate of the Chabad Centers of Coral Springs). 2739542.name: Congregation Judea Chabad

3011301.name: Young Israel Chabad

4035363.name: Chabad of Downtown SRQ

6388831.name: Chabad of Summit
6388831.note: COLlive, 19 March 2024: 'The city of Summit, New Jersey now has its first Chabad Shliach'; Rabbi Mendy and Chana Marasow 'have opened up the first Chabad center, local to Summit'.

118547.name: Chabad of Randolph
118547.note: WRNJ (6 Jan 2026): 'Founded in 1987, Chabad of Randolph has served the township's growing Jewish community for decades'; its 3,000 sq ft complex on Hanover Avenue opened in 2023 (now the Hadar Family Foundation Center). Rabbi Avraham and Chava Bekhor today; reportedly begun by his mother, Devora Tilson, in her home.

118550.name: Chabad of Sussex County
118550.note: Sparta Independent (Nov 2017): 'Chabad of Sussex County, located at 266 Woodport Road in Sparta, was established in 2002'; Rabbi Mendel Dubov has led it since about 2011 (a Rabbi Lewis led it in 2006). In 2006 it moved into a Sparta plaza (CrownHeights.info).

118577.name: Chabad of Princeton University
118577.note: Several accounts: Rabbi Eitan Webb 'founded the Chabad House at Princeton in 2002'; he and Gitty Webb 'began Princeton's Chabad in 2002 in a narrow apartment near Nassau Street'; Jewish Link (2024): they arrived 'to launch the Scharf Family Chabad House 22 years ago'. In spring 2020 it bought the adjacent 17 Edwards Place.

earlier.where: a narrow apartment near Nassau Street

118587.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Monroe
118587.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 Oct 2015: 'As the Hakhel year began, just after Rosh Hashanah, hundreds filled the hall in celebration of the 13th anniversary' of the Chabad Jewish Center of Monroe Township (so fall 2002); a 2004 report: Rabbi Eliezer Zaklikovsky 'was sent to Monroe to start a new Chabad center about two years ago'. IRS: active from Feb 2003. (Its 10th-anniversary gala was held in Oct 2013.)

118603.name: Chabad of Hunterdon County
118603.note: CrownHeights.info, 8 June 2013: 'On Wednesday, May 29th Chabad of Hunterdon County celebrated its 10th Anniversary Dinner Banquet'; a 2009 banquet marked its sixth anniversary; elsewhere 'established in 2003 by Rabbi Eli and Rachel Kornfeld'. (One article and the IRS record say 2004.) Now in Annandale/Clinton Township.

118627.name: Chabad in Medford
118627.note: Burlington County Times (CrownHeights.info, 24 March 2014): Rabbi Yitzchok Kahan 'arrived in South Jersey 10 years ago, and used his small home as a meeting place and quasi-synagogue'; the Inquirer (June 2015): the group grew from fewer than 10 people meeting 12 years earlier at the Medford Community Center or Masonic Lodge (so 2003); another piece has him joining in 2007. New home on Main Street (74 S. Main St.) in 2014.

earlier.where: the Kahans' home; also the Medford Community Center and the local Masonic Lodge

150720.name: Chabad of Toms River
150720.note: Chabad.org: the Chabad House 'was founded in 2004'; Rabbi Moshe Gourarie (interview): cold calls starting in 2004; the Forward (2016): it had operated from the rabbi's home for 12 years when told it needed a variance. Began in a small house on New Hampshire Avenue; later the rabbi's home at 2001 Church Road (bought 2011). IRS entity: 2007.

earlier.where: a small house on New Hampshire Avenue
the rabbi's home, 2001 Church Road

416264.name: Chabad of Old Tappan
416264.note: The Jewish Standard (CrownHeights.info, about 30 June 2006, 'The Rebbe's New Soldier: Chabad to Open in Old Tappan'): Lubavitch on the Palisades will sponsor Rabbi Mendy Lewis to start a Chabad outpost in Old Tappan later that summer, serving Northvale, Rockleigh and Harrington Park; Anash (2024): a housewarming marking '18 years of Chabad Old Tappan'.

555228.name: Chabad of Gloucester County
555228.note: Chabad of Gloucester County 'was founded in 2007 by Rabbi Avi & Mina Richler'; Rabbi Richler (2017): 'When we came in 2007 to Gloucester County, we knew one Jewish family'. A permanent home (a former bed-and-breakfast in the historic district, 12 Woodstown Road) from 2011.

259220.name: Chabad of Northwest NJ - Western Region
259220.note: Recorder Community Newspapers (CrownHeights.info, 7 Nov 2007), on Rabbi Yaacov Shusterman's Chabad Jewish Center in Flanders (Mount Olive): 'The Chabad's Hebrew school ... started out as two students attending in 2004'; in 2007 the center was 'in its third year'; High Holiday services at the Flanders Crossing Recreation Center.

749411.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Holmdel
749411.note: New Jersey Jewish News (CrownHeights.info, 27 Oct 2008): Chabad of Western Monmouth County 'has established an outreach center for students attending Brookdale Community College. The new Chabad Jewish Center, which opened in early October, is located in the Holmdel residence of Rabbi Shmaya Galperin'; Asbury Park Press (CrownHeights.info, 10 March 2011): 'When I first came here three years ago ... I had only 20 people on the High Holy Days'. Later at 65 West Main Street.

earlier.where: Rabbi Shmaya Galperin's Holmdel residence

1418905.name: Anshei Lubavitch
1418905.note: Jewish Link (1 Nov 2017): 'Anshei Lubavitch, which was founded in 1909, has a number of sifrei Torah ... according to Rabbi Neubort, the shul's rabbi'. A business listing says it formed from a merger of three Paterson synagogues and moved to Fair Lawn in 1985. The year is the congregation's founding; when it came under a Chabad rabbi (Rabbi Levi Neubort) is not found.

earlier.where: Paterson, N.J. (before the move to Fair Lawn)

2021658.name: Chabad of Montclair
2021658.note: Baristanet (CrownHeights.info, 15 Sept 2014): Rabbi Yaacov and Ita Leaf 'are hoping to establish a Chabad presence in Montclair'; 'The Leafs moved to Montclair in July, from Crown Heights'; appointed by her father, Rabbi Boruch Klar of West Orange (ChabadInfo, 13 Sept 2014). Now 9 Carriage Way.

2298429.name: Chabad at Rowan University
2298429.note: Jewish Link (Sept 2024): the university 'has had a Chabad for 11 years since Rabbi Hersh Loschak and his wife, Fraidy, came to campus' (so 2013); Courier-Post (via AOL): the center 'celebrated its 10th year' in April 2023.

2676928.name: Chabad Community Center of Robbinsville and S. Hamilton
2676928.note: CrownHeights.info: 'Rabbi Chaiton and his wife Chana moved to Hamilton in 5774 – 2014, under the umbrella of Chabad of Mercer County' (her father, Rabbi Dovid Dubov); NJ Jewish News: the couple opened the Chabad house in Robbinsville in 2014, at first holding ceremonies at their home; the ninth center under Chabad of Mercer County.

earlier.where: the Chaitons' home

1539663.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life | Upper Passaic County
1539663.note: Jewish Standard (23 Sept 2011): Rabbi Mendy Gurkov's new Chabad Jewish Center of Upper Passaic County 'officially opened on Sept. 15 with a wine tasting and kabbalah lecture held at the Holiday Inn in Wanaque', holding events there or at the Gurkovs' home at first; later rented space in the Haskell Town Shopping Center, and a permanent home in 2024 (Jewish Link).

earlier.where: the Holiday Inn, Wanaque, and the Gurkovs' home
rented space in the Haskell Town Shopping Center

3186402.name: Chabad of West Orange
3186402.note: NJ Jewish News (2 July 2014): 'In 1996, before founding West Orange Chabad, Rabbi Boruch Klar and his wife, Devorah, opened a store' (Lubavitch Center Judaica, 456 Pleasant Valley Way); 'Three years later, they began running a beginners' service at Ahawas Achim B'nai Jacob & David' (1999); 'Within two years the service outgrew its space in that synagogue and moved to the store's basement'; Rabbi Mendy and Altie Kasowitz were hired to grow it. Its own building, 401 Pleasant Valley Way, was dedicated on June 14 (2015).

earlier.where: a beginners' service at Ahawas Achim B'nai Jacob & David
the basement of Lubavitch Center Judaica, 456 Pleasant Valley Way

2941342.name: Shabbat House
2941342.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 27 Nov 2017): 'The Klars began mapping out their plans for the Shabbat House in 2015, with the facility officially opening in August 2016.'

3423247.name: Chabad of South Bergen County and The Meadowlands
3423247.note: Jewish Standard (28 Sept 2014): Rabbi Yitzchok Lerman, 'who is affiliated with Chabad', is 'the new religious leader of Temple Beth-El in Rutherford'; he renamed it Congregation Beth-El Chabad, base of Chabad of South Bergen and the Meadowlands. The shul (founded 1919 as South Bergen Hebrew Institute, not Chabad) burned down on 8 Aug 2025.

earlier.where: Temple (Congregation) Beth-El, Rutherford (the same shul before it was Chabad; destroyed by fire 2025)

3235800.name: Chabad of Jackson
3235800.note: Lubavitch.com, 12 Sept 2016: 'Rabbi Shmulie and Musi Naparstek are moving to Jackson, New Jersey with their two daughters to open a new branch of Chabad'.

117656.name: Lubavitch Center of Essex County
117656.note: Jewish Link: their daughter Ita Leaf grew up in West Orange, 'where her parents have served as the directors of Chabad of Essex County since 1980' (Rabbi Boruch and Devorah Klar). The Lubavitch Center Judaica store at 456 Pleasant Valley Way opened in 1996; IRS ruling 2004.

3779812.name: Chabad of Closter
3779812.note: The center's own 'Meet Our Family' page: Rabbi Yossi Gluckowsky, invited by Rabbi Mordechai Shain (Lubavitch on the Palisades), founded the Closter shul in 2017. IRS ruling for its corporation 2019.

4173417.name: Chabad of Bayonne
4173417.note: Jewish Link: Rabbi Moshe and Chaya Schapiro (Hoboken) led intermittent activities in Bayonne 'until 2017, when Rabbi Yisrael and Shulamis Bennish came to establish a permanent Chabad house'.

earlier.where: Bayonne activities run from Chabad of Hoboken (Rabbi Moshe Schapiro)

4016283.name: Chabad of Hackensack
4016283.note: Jewish Link, 11 April 2018, 'First-Ever Chabad House to Open in Hackensack': just before Pesach Friends of Lubavitch of Bergen County agreed to acquire Temple Beth El's building at 280 Summit Avenue; 'the newly forming Chabad of Hackensack ... will be led by Rabbi Mendy Kaminker, who is moving to Hackensack in June from southern New Jersey'.

117992.name: Chabad Center of Passaic County
117992.note: TAPinto Wayne (Sept 2022, listed on lubavitch.com In the Media 29 Sept 2022), 'The Chabad Center in Wayne Celebrates 30 Years - Opening of New Pre-School': close to 200 supporters on Sunday 9/11 (2022) marked a new Torah, a new preschool and the 30th year of Chabad's presence in Passaic County. Its corporation, Chabad Torah Center of Passaic County Inc (194 Ratzer Rd, EIN 22-3134870), has an IRS ruling of April 1993, which agrees. Rabbi Michel and Chani Gurkov.

3205782.name: Chabad of Stockton University
3205782.note: CrownHeights.info, 13 Sept 2016, from NJ.com: 'Rabbi Meir Rapoport and his wife Shaina are opening a Chabad Jewish Center in Galloway to serve the Jewish student community at Stockton University'. Lubavitch.com later: they arrived in Galloway in the fall of 2016 and first rented a small home; the center bought 118 E Jimmie Leeds Road later.

5572424.name: Chabad of Dumont
5572424.note: Jewish Link, 1 Feb 2023, 'Chabad Opens in Dumont': Rabbi Avrohom and Leah Engel are moving from Fair Lawn to Dumont to establish a new Chabad Jewish Center; 'After spending a few months meeting and introducing themselves to the local residents, the Engels coordinated the first Chanukah menorah lighting celebration in Dumont in many years in December', hosted by the Borough of Dumont and Chabad Dumont. Jewish Link, 16 March 2023: Chabad of Dumont 'currently in formation'; the Engels prepare to move to Dumont after Pesach (2023).

earlier.where: Run from the Engels' home in Fair Lawn

7011141.name: Chabad Cherry Hill West
7011141.note: Its own About Us page: 'Chabad of Cherry Hill West was established in 2025, to serve the Jewish community of Cherry Hill's West Side'; Rabbi Isser and Leah Brikman. CrownHeights.info, 23 Aug 2025: the West Side of Cherry Hill 'will be getting its first Chabad center' (the 73rd in New Jersey).

5837382.name: Chabad of Northwest NJ - Berkshire Valley
5837382.note: CrownHeights.info, 1 Aug 2023, 'Welcome The New Shluchim to the Skylands Region of New Jersey': Rabbi Levi and Chaya Naparstek 'will be moving out on Shlichus to the Skylands region of New Jersey to open a new Chabad House', under Rabbi Asher Herson (Chabad of Northwest NJ); Berkshire Valley, Wharton and Netcong among the towns.

5154678.name: Chabad of the Caldwells
5154678.note: Patch (Caldwells), 17 March 2026: 'Rabbi Sputz and Gittel relocated to the Caldwells in 2022, stepping into a community where they initially knew no one' (Rabbi Shmuly and Gittel Sputz, founders of Chabad of the Caldwells).

4544696.name: Chabad of Florence
4544696.note: COLlive, 17 July 2019, 'Shluchim Open New Jersey's 60th Chabad Center': 'Rabbi Shmuel and Mushky Wilhelm have recently founded Chabad of Florence, NJ, and will serve as the Shluchim to Bordentown, Florence and Burlington Townships' (they had directed the Friendship Circle of Mercer County for 10 years).

3058083.name: Chabad Young Professionals of Hoboken and Jersey City
3058083.note: Chabad.org via CrownHeights.info, 30 May 2024: 'in 2015, Rabbi Shmully and Esta Levitin established Chabad Young Professionals of Hoboken and Jersey City'. Jewish Link, 6 April 2017 ('Hudson County Young Jewish Professionals Choose Chabad'): 'About a year and a half ago' the Schapiros enlisted the Levitins to start it (so about fall 2015).

7328051.name: Chabad of Maplewood/South Orange (SOMA)
7328051.note: Its own About page (Beth Ephraim-Maplewood Jewish Center): the shul has served Maplewood and South Orange 'Since 1961'; 'In 1995, he [Rabbi Sholom Bogomilsky] and his wife Frumie commuted from their home in Brooklyn to be part of the Center's leadership', and it now runs 'In keeping with the Chabad approach'. The year is when Chabad's leadership began; the congregation itself is from 1961.

4961934.name: Chabad Passaic Clifton
4961934.note: Jewish Link, 16 March 2017: 'On February 26, Chabad of Passaic-Clifton held its annual dinner, celebrating 10 years of making a difference' (Rabbi Yitzchak and Miriam Sebbag), so about 2007. Its corporation Chabad of Passaic Clifton Inc has an IRS ruling of Aug 2010. One count-back only.

118395.name: Chabad of Freehold
118395.note: CrownHeights.info, 23 May 2006 (Chabad of Western Monmouth's 20 years): 'The Bernsteins moved to western Monmouth County in January 1994 to help expand Chabad outreach programs ... rabbi Bernstein and Mrs. Bernstein serve as the Chabad rabbi and rebbetzin for the Freehold Jewish community.' When the Freehold branch itself began is not stated: after Jan 1994, by 2006.

7446707.name: Chabad of West Philadelphia
7446707.note: COLlive, 25 Aug 2026: 'Rabbi Mendel and Mushka Dubrowski will be moving on the Rebbe's Shlichus to start a New Chabad House in the community of West Philadelphia, PA.'

117957.name: Lubavitch of Center City
117957.note: Wikipedia (Historic Congregation B'nai Abraham, 523-527 Lombard Street, officially B'nai Abraham Chabad, home of Lubavitch of Center City): 'Rabbi Yochonon Goldman became the congregation's rabbi in 2000'. COLlive, 9 April 2024: Rabbi Yochonon and Leah Goldman 'have been leading the community over the past 24 years', which agrees; the Jewish Exponent (search snippet) dates their appointment as emissaries to Philadelphia to January 2000. The congregation itself is much older; the year is when Chabad's leadership began. Leah Goldman founded the Center City Jewish Preschool in 2001.

118473.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Lehigh Valley
118473.note: Its own Idealist profile: Rabbi Yaakov and Devorah Halperin 'established Chabad Lubavitch of the Lehigh Valley in Allentown, Pennsylvania in 2001'. It first met in their home; a new center was dedicated in 2009 (search summaries).

118495.name: Chabad of Penn State
118495.note: Penn State News, 28 Oct 2019: the Meretskys 'will celebrate 18 years on campus'; Rabbi Nosson Meretsky: 'We first arrived on the Penn State campus on 11 September 2001'. CrownHeights.info (Daily Collegian Q&A), 2 Dec 2012: 'We've been here 11 years. This will be our 12th annual menorah lighting', which agrees.

118357.name: Chabad of the Main Line
118357.note: Its own Idealist profile: 'Opened in 1999, Chabad of the Main Line', now 'at the historic General Wayne Inn' in Merion Station (Rabbi Shraga Sherman). It began in a storefront on Montgomery Avenue (and was in Bala Cynwyd in 2005); the General Wayne Inn center opened 31 Jan 2007 (Jewish Exponent via CrownHeights.info).

earlier.where: Storefront on Montgomery Avenue; Bala Cynwyd (2005)

118619.name: Chabad Lubavitch of The Poconos
118619.note: Chabad.org, 9 Nov 2007 ('Mountain Region Chabad House Symbol of Exurbs' Growth Nationwide'): 'Rabbi Mendel Bendet, the young co-director of the four-year-old Chabad-Lubavitch of the Poconos' (so about 2003). One count-back; therebbesimpact.com also has the Bendets 2003 (a lead).

319750.name: Rohr Chabad Jewish Center
319750.note: LancasterOnline (CrownHeights.info, 14 July 2013): 'Green, a Pittsburgh native, came to Lancaster in 2003, when Rabbi Shaya Sackett, of Congregation Degel Israel, invited him to teach Hebrew half time ... Green devoted the other half of his workday to establishing a local branch of Chabad'; the Chabad Jewish Enrichment Center first shared the Greens' home on Race Avenue, and the Rohr center at 1024 Harrisburg Pike opened in 2013. York Daily Record (Oct 2007): they 'moved to Lancaster three years ago and started the Chabad Jewish Enrichment Center' (about 2004). IRS: Chabad of Lancaster Inc, ruling July 2005.

earlier.where: The Greens' home on Race Avenue, Lancaster

562076.name: Chabad of York, PA
562076.note: York Daily Record (CrownHeights.info, 18 Oct 2007), 'Chabad to Open Jewish Outreach Center': Rabbi Elazar Green's Chabad Jewish Enrichment Center of Lancaster & York 'has purchased a house in Spring Garden Township near York College' that 'will become York County's first Chabad House'; he had looked for a house in York for three years. The chabad.org listing (562076) is from about 2007, which agrees.

118217.name: Lubavitch of Montgomery County
118217.note: CrownHeights.info, 4 July 2007: 'Lubavitch of Montgomery County has operated for 10 years now, but programs have taken place all over' (Rabbi Shaya and Devorah Leah Deitsch; so about 1997). IRS: Lubavitch Of Montgomery County, ruling Oct 2000, which allows it. One count-back only.

118280.note: Chabad.org, 4 Jan 2011 ('Suburban Synagogue and Mosque Sit Side by Side'): 'In 1998, he [Rabbi Yossi Kaplan] was in Brooklyn, looking for a place to start a Chabad House'; the family first rented a home and other space for programs; 'by September 2000, they were able to rent what he described as a huge building' in Berwyn; the Devon property was bought in Dec 2002. IRS: ruling April 2001. So it began after 1998 and by Sept 2000.

118420.name: Chabad of the Abingtons - Jewish Discovery Center
118420.note: COLlive, 11 April 2021: Rabbi Benny and Chany Rapoport, shluchim to Clarks Summit and the Abingtons, 'have been serving the local Jewish community since arriving in 2001'. A chabad.org profile (search summary, not checked) says fall 2000. IRS: Chabad Of The Abingtons Inc, ruling May 2002. The Jewish Discovery Center at 749 Northern Blvd opened in 2003; now 216 Miller Road, Waverly. The two sources differ by a year: medium.

118237.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Berks County
118237.note: Reading Eagle (CrownHeights.info, 15 Feb 2009): Congregation Shomrei Habrith, 2310 Hampden Blvd, became the Chabad Center; 'Rabbi Yosef Lipsker, who has been the congregation's rabbi since 1997, will stay on as Chabad rabbi'. IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Of Berks County Inc, ruling Jan 2008. When Chabad of Berks County itself began (1997 or later) is not stated.

117713.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Harrisburg
117713.note: IRS: Chabad-Lubavitch Congregation Of Harrisburg (3515 Green St), ruling May 1993, so it existed by then. Encyclopaedia Judaica lists 'Machzike Hadas (1904), now known as Chabad-Lubavitch' among Harrisburg's congregations. Rabbi Shmuel Pewzner's start is not found.

117880.name: Lubavitch of Bucks County
117880.note: About 1993, counted back twice. The Jewish Exponent, 30 Aug 2023: 'The Lubavitch of Bucks County started in Yardley 30 years ago but moved to Newtown'; its own site's 'Branding' page (from about 2017-18) speaks of 'The 25th anniversary milestone'. The Philadelphia Inquirer (CrownHeights.info, 6 Oct 2005): the $1.5 million Glazier Jewish Center in a former Baptist church in Newtown Borough opened on the eve of Rosh Hashanah 2005, Rabbi Yehuda Shemtov executive director. No source states the year itself: medium.

earlier.where: Yardley (where it started)

2761055.name: Chabad of North Pocono
2761055.note: IRS: Chabad Of North Pocono (947 Clay Ave, Scranton), ruling March 2020, so it existed by then. Mitzvah Mobile; Rabbi Mendel Raices. Lead: therebbesimpact.com has Mendel & Chaya Raices 2011; the chabad.org listing (2761055) is from about 2014.

117945.name: Chabad House @ University of Pennsylvania
117945.note: The Lubavitch House at Penn (4032-34 Spruce Street, now the Perelman Center for Jewish Life): the Daily Pennsylvanian (June 2016) says it 'opened in 1980 to serve as the University's Chabad house'; JNS's author note: Rabbi Menachem Schmidt 'established the Lubavitch House at the University of Pennsylvania in 1980'; Schmidt: when they launched it in 1980 there were eight full-time campus Chabad Houses in America. (One source says 1979.) Rabbi Ephraim Levin is listed for it today.

744158.name: Chabad at Lehigh University
744158.note: The Brown and White (Lehigh), 19 Oct 2016: 'Zalman Greenberg decided to create Chabad at Lehigh in 2008'; another Brown and White profile: in July 2008 Dit and Zalman Greenberg moved to Bethlehem. The former Kulik Funeral Home became its center (Joachim Schaufeld Center for Jewish Life) in 2016.

1337772.name: Chabad Serving Drexel University - Rohr Jewish Student Center
1337772.note: CrownHeights.info and COLlive, 14 Nov 2010, 'New Shluchim to Drexel University': Rabbi Chaim and Moussia Goldstein; they first gave Torah classes and a few months later moved to Philadelphia to establish a permanent Chabad presence at Drexel. The chabad.org listing (1337772) is from Nov 2010, which agrees.

420369.name: Rohr Center for Jewish Life - Chabad House
420369.note: Times of Israel blog (Allan Ripp, 7 Oct 2025): Rabbi Eli Gurevitz 'first arrived at the Quaker-founded school in 2006'; 'When my wife and I first arrived in 2006', perhaps among the first full-time Chabad operations at a small liberal-arts college; an alumnus urged him to 'pack it in after 17 years' (about 2023). Serves Haverford, Bryn Mawr and Swarthmore. The chabad.org listing (420369) is from about 2006, which agrees.

484384.name: The Stanley Middleman Center for Jewish Life - Rohr Chabad @ Temple University
484384.note: Its own campaign 'Jewish Owls Turn 10!': 'the Kantor Family joined the Temple University Family the 2007-2008 school year'; '10 YEARS HAVE GONE BY!!!'. Rabbi Baruch S. Kantor, 1428 N Broad Street.

4809936.name: Old City Jewish Arts Center
4809936.note: Old City District listing: 'Founded in 2006, the OCJAC was envisioned as a platform to build Jewish community through the arts.' CrownHeights.info, 18 Dec 2013: Rabbi Menachem Schmidt 'started the Old City Jewish Art Center ... about seven years ago', which agrees. Co-director today Rabbi Zalman Shimon Wircberg.

6670209.name: Chabad of Media
6670209.note: CrownHeights.info, 19 March 2025: 'Rabbi Avraham and Chanie Deitsch have moved to Media, Pennsylvania to launch a new Chabad center in the city - and the fourth in the county'.

2752570.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Northern Delaware County
2752570.note: CrownHeights.info, 19 March 2025: Rabbi Tzvi and Rikki Altein 'who've been serving Chabad of Delaware County, Pennsylvania for the past decade' (so about 2015). The chabad.org listing (2752570) is from about 2014-15. One count-back only.

5386600.name: Chabad West Shore Jewish Center
5386600.note: COLlive, 10 Aug 2022: 'Rabbi Nissen and Chana Pewzner (Kosofsky) and their baby ... moved on Shlichus to Cumberland County, PA ... The Pewzners will be establishing the Chabad west shore Jewish Center'.

6021390.name: Swarthmore Chabad
6021390.note: COLlive, 30 July 2023: 'Rabbi Mordi and Reizel Wolf (nee Garelik) are the new Shluchim to Swarthmore College'; Tri-Co Chabad (Rabbi Eli and Blumie Gurevitz) 'entrusted Swarthmore College to the Wolfs to branch out and establish an independent Chabad House'.

117715.name: Lubavitcher Center
117715.note: Philadelphia City Paper (COLlive, 28 Aug 2009): 'Philadelphia became one of the first major U.S. cities with an outpost when Rabbi Avrohom Shemtov began his mission here in 1961, out in the far Northeast on Castor Avenue, where he still resides.' (The Lubavitcher Center, NE Philadelphia; Shemtov also began Torah classes on campus in 1962.)

425767.name: Jewish Center of Northern Liberties
425767.note: Philadelphia City Paper (COLlive, 28 Aug 2009): the Lag B'Omer event 'began in 2005 and Rabbi Gedaliah Lowenstein, who leads the Jewish Center of Northern Liberties across the street - which opened that same year'. The chabad.org listing (425767) is from about 2006, which agrees.

1337491.name: Chabad of Lafayette Hill
1337491.note: Chabad.org, 19 Nov 2010 ('New Centers Cater to Art Students, Suburbanites'): 'Rabbi Yisroel and Chaya Kotlarsky are setting up shop in the upscale community of Lafayette Hill', among the centers opened in the previous six months. The chabad.org listing (1337491) is from Nov 2010, which agrees.

1304267.name: Chabad House for Students
1304267.note: Chabad.org, 19 Nov 2010 ('New Centers Cater to Art Students, Suburbanites'): Rabbi Daniel and Reuvena Leah Grodnitzky are newly 'running programs for students at a cluster of art schools' downtown, where 'There was no Jewish programming yet for them' (Rabbi Menachem Schmidt); the new Philadelphia Chabad Houses 'are just getting started'. Philadelphia Inquirer (2019): they bought 1601 Lombard in 2012.

3757460.name: Chabad of Fairmount
3757460.note: Its own home page: 'Chabad of Fairmount, established in 2017 offers youth programs, adult education', under Rabbi Hirshi and Shevy Sputz. The chabad.org listing (3757460) is from about 2017, which agrees.

3027498.name: PSJews - Chabad of the Undergrads
3027498.note: Its own home page: 'In 2015, just newly married, we moved from Toronto to Happy Valley and are now the home for hundreds of PSJews' (Rabbi Hershy Gourarie and his wife). The chabad.org listing (3027498) is from about 2015, which agrees.

5381238.name: Chabad of Lords Valley
5381238.note: Its own home page: 'Established in 2016, Chabad of Lords Valley serves the greater Hemlock Farms area.' Rabbi Shmuel Shur (per chabad.org). The chabad.org listing (5381238) dates only from about 2022.

6358286.name: Bala Chabad
6358286.note: Its own 'About Our Center' page: 'Since its humble beginnings in 2021, BALA CHABAD has quickly garnered a reputation'.

6642528.name: Chabad Lubavitch NE Philadelphia Jewish Education Center
6642528.note: Its own About page: 'In 2024, this center was established to enrich Jewish education, outreach, and community connection' (Rabbi Mendel and Moussia Gansburg).

118521.name: Lubavitch Center for Russian Jewry
118521.note: Its own site (LubavitchBustleton.org): 'The Lubavitch Center for Russian Jewry, founded in 2001'. Rabbi Sholom Goldshmid (per chabad.org).

117717.name: Chabad of Penn Wynne
117717.note: The Jewish Exponent (CrownHeights.info, 8 Feb 2007): 'A new Torah scroll was completed recently for Chabad of Penn Wynne'; the procession went from the Kaiserman JCC in Wynnewood 'to the ark at the Chabad House on the corner of Haverford Road and Indian Creek Drive' (Rabbi Zalman Gerber). So it existed by early 2007; its start is not stated. Wikipedia (Penn Wynne; no citation): it started in Rabbi Gerber's house, moved to a storefront on Manoa Road soon after Congregation Beth Hamedrosh moved in across the street in 2007, left it when the lease ended in late May 2010, held Shabbat services in the JCC's Family Hall from 5 June 2010, and from Rosh Hashana (Sept) 2020 has been across City Line Avenue in Overbrook Park (now 7571 Haverford Ave). Rabbi Moshe and Devorah Brennan have directed it since 2011 (its About page).

earlier.where: Wynnewood: Rabbi Zalman Gerber's house, the Chabad House at Haverford Road and Indian Creek Drive
Wynnewood: a storefront on Manoa Road, across from Congregation Beth Hamedrosh
Wynnewood: Shabbat services in the Family Hall of the Kaiserman JCC

119652.name: Gan Israel Camps & Youth Services
119652.note: Camp Gan Israel of Greater Philadelphia (the Rose and Morris Caskey Gan Israel Camps; its campsite is in Collegeville), Rabbi Zalman and Miriam Gerber. Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 17 April 2014): 'For 25 years, he has run a day camp.' COLlive (24 May 2020): 'Rabbi Zalman and Miriam Gerber were sent by the Rebbe over 30 years ago to Philadelphia, and at the specific direction of the Rebbe bought a beautiful 10 acre campsite.' Both count back to about 1989. Its own 'About Our Camp' page dates from 1 June 2005.

117731.name: Chabad Lubavitch Center Regional Hdqts.
117731.note: Lubavitch.com, 11 March 2003 ('A 30th B-day for Chabad of the Lone Star State'): Chabad Lubavitch of Texas 'celebrated 30 years in the state' on 9 March 2003; 'in 1972, when Rabbi Shimon and Chiena Lazaroff ... came to Houston'. The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 section on Chabad's 50 years in Texas (ChabadInfo, 'Chabad's 50-year Lone Star Journey'): 'When the Lazaroffs first arrived in Houston on May 10, 1972'; construction of the center on Fondren Road (the first Chabad center built from the ground up) began in 1977 and it opened for the High Holy Days in 1978 (CrownHeights.info, Jan 2007, says the center was founded in 1976); before that, an apartment.

117728.name: Chabad of Dallas
117728.note: Its own About page: 'In 1984, Rabbi Mendel and Baila Dubrawsky were inspired by the Rebbe's vision' and settled in Dallas, starting with small classes, Shabbat meals and holiday celebrations. The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history (ChabadInfo) agrees: 'In 1984, Rabbi Mendel and Baila Dubrawsky went to Dallas.' Against: COLlive (May 2021) has them arriving in 1985.

117727.name: Chabad of Austin
117727.note: Chabad of Texas's 50-year history (Jewish Herald-Voice, 2022, on ChabadInfo): 'In 1980, Rabbi Traxler and his wife, Shoshana, were appointed as shluchim of Chabad in Austin' (Rabbi Moishe Traxler had been one of the first UT students involved with Chabad, from 1972). The Jewish Outlook (Shalom Austin, June 2024, 'Journey of Growth'): the story of Chabad in Austin began in 1973 with Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff's trips from Houston to teach UT students; 'Nearly a decade later, Rabbi Yosef Levertov moved to Austin at the invitation of the then UT rabbi, Rabbi Traxler'; 'In 1984, Rabbi Yosef Levertov and his wife Rochel Levertov moved to Austin to join Chabad Lubavitch of Austin and two years later they were given the keys.' So the center was there before the Levertovs: its own About page dates its journey from their arrival in 1984 ('Our journey in Austin commenced in 1984'). The Traxlers then moved to Houston (Chabad Outreach of Houston).

117926.name: Chabad of Plano/Collin County
117926.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Plano founded in 1992'; 'over the past 30 years, Chabad of Plano has grown'; its gallery has a '2022 Event - Celebrating 30 Years'. (Lubavitch.com, March 2003, lists Plano among the centers established from Houston.)

118556.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Fort Worth & Tarrant County
118556.note: Its own home page: 'In September of 2002, Chabad Headquarters in Texas' appointed Rabbi Dov and Chana Tovah Mandel directors of Chabad activities in Tarrant County. Lubavitch.com (March 2003) already lists Fort Worth among the centers established from Houston.

2456591.name: Chabad of Frisco
2456591.note: The Frisco Enterprise (CrownHeights.info, 17 Sept 2015): Rabbi Mendy and Mushkie Kesselman 'moved from New York to Frisco ... in August 2014'. COLlive (18 Nov 2014, after Chabad.org): they 'moved to Texas to build their own Chabad community in the town of Frisco' (Mushkie is the daughter of Plano's Rabbi Menachem and Rivka Block).

4026720.name: Chabad of Cypress
4026720.note: COLlive, 30 Aug 2018 (after Chabad.org, 27 Aug 2018, 'Hurricane Harvey Anniversary Gift: A New Chabad Center'): 'The 12th Chabad center in the Houston area, to be co-directed by Rabbi Levi and Devorah Leah Marinovsky, was timed to start by the anniversary of Hurricane Harvey'.

4476658.name: Chabad of Allen-McKinney
4476658.note: Lubavitch.com, 4 Oct 2019 ('Fiftieth Chabad in the Lone Star State'): 'In October, Rabbi Sholom and Chaya Block will be ... setting out to serve the Jewish communities in Allen and McKinney, Texas', the fiftieth Chabad couple in Texas. Today Rabbi Eli and Nechama Newman run Chabad of Allen-McKinney (ChabadAM.org); the chabad.org listing (4476658) is from about 2019. That the Newmans took over the Blocks' center isn't stated anywhere found: medium.

5381032.name: Chabad of Boerne
5381032.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 23 Aug 2023): 'in Boerne, Texas, a fledgling Chabad center is led by Rabbi Yossi and Malkie Marrus', with Chabad of San Antonio since 1997; 'in 2021 they left San Antonio's ... winding roads for the longhorn cattle ranches of Boerne'.

5587788.name: Chabad of Leander
5587788.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 23 Dec 2024, 'Chabad Opens in Leander, Texas, Amid Tech-Fueled Boom'): a family that moved to Leander in 2021 heard, 'two years after moving to town', of its first-ever public menorah lighting, 'held by Rabbi Shmuly and Nechomele Levertov, who'd just moved to town to found Chabad of Leander' (so about 2023). The year is worked out, not stated: medium.

6262181.name: Chabad of Carrollton-Lewisville
6262181.note: COLlive, 17 Sept 2024: 'For the past 18 years, Rabbi Yudi and Esther Horowitz have been on Shlichus in Plano, Texas. Now, they are heading out to establish Chabad of Carrollton-Lewisville in North Texas', with the approval of Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky.

118570.name: Chabad of Sugar Land
118570.note: COLlive, 6 Sept 2010: 'On Sunday, August 29, Chabad of Sugar Land, Texas, led by Rabbi Mendel and Chaya Feigenson, celebrated their 10th anniversary at their annual dinner' (count back: 2000). Its site calls the Feigensons its 'Founding Rabbi and Directors'. An anniversary count: medium.

1392216.name: The Shul of Bellaire
1392216.note: Chabad.org, 6 April 2016 ('Bellaire, Texas: A Magnet for Jewish Families in Southwest Houston'): Rabbi Yossi Zaklikofsky says the family moved to Bellaire at the end of 2010; the 2016 gala marked 'Five years of Jewish growth at The Shul of Bellaire' (the shul from about 2011). Before that they were appointed to Pearland (CrownHeights.info, 8 Dec 2008: to 'establish a new Chabad House serving ... Alvin, Friendswood and Pearland').

1324719.name: Chabad of The Woodlands
1324719.note: Chabad.org, 2 Sept 2013 ('Big Cattle, Big Hats and a Bigger Chabad Center'): Rabbi Mendel and Leah Blecher 'came to the community in 2011', working out of their home at first. CrownHeights.info (5 Feb 2014) agrees: the growth 'since he founded Chabad of The Woodlands three years ago'.

397245.name: Chabad of the Rio Grande Valley
397245.note: CrownHeights.info, 17 May 2010: 'Rabbi Asher and Dini Hecht ... have recently moved on Shlichus to the Rio Grande Valley of Texas where they will be establishing a new Chabad center', appointed by Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff. But chabad.org already listed Chabad of the Rio Grande Valley (397245, a listing from about 2005) beside a July 2007 report on Camp Gan Israel on South Padre Island, so there was something under that name before the Hechts: medium.

1090905.name: Camp Gan Israel South Padre Island Texas
1090905.note: Lubavitch.com (3 Aug 2006, 'Experimental Camp A Success'; also CrownHeights.info, 30 July 2006): Camp Gan Israel on South Padre Island's '2006 summer session' was its first: 'this newly founded camp is a longtime dream of Rabbis Asher Hecht and Eli Laber'; 'The theme of this inaugural summer was an instructive-based water camp'; 'In this inaugural year' it took only Texas children. Chabad.org (11 July 2007) describes its next summer. Rabbi Asher Hecht (Chabad of the Rio Grande Valley) directs it.

117919.name: Chabad at Texas Medical Center
117919.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 31 Aug 2011, 'Houston Patients Find a Caring Embrace in Aishel House'): 'The Lazaroffs launched what would eventually become the Aishel House in 1992, not long after moving to the area around the medical center' (Rabbi Eliezer and Rochel Lazaroff); in 1995 they added a two-bedroom apartment as its first hospitality department, and in 2003 the center bought an adjacent 18-unit apartment building.

earlier.where: a two-bedroom apartment beside the Medical Center (its first hospitality department)

512666.name: Rohr Chabad Jewish Center at Texas A&M University
512666.note: CrownHeights.info, 30 April 2007 ('New Shluchim to Texas'): 'Rabbi Yossi and Manya Lazaroff will IYH be moving on Shlichus to College Station, Texas where they will establish a new Chabad House serving the students and faculty at Texas A&M University', appointed by Chabad of Texas. Chabad.org's news on it starts in July 2007.

536472.name: The Igor Tulchinsky Chabad Campus at the University of Texas at Austin
536472.note: The Jewish Outlook (CrownHeights.info, 6 Aug 2007): 'Rabbi Zev Johnson and his wife, Ariela, are co-directing Chabad House, Rabbi Yosef and Rochel Levertov announced. The Johnsons arrived in June' to manage Chabad's campus activities at the University of Texas. The year is the campus center's own directors'; Chabad at UT itself goes back to the Levertovs (1984, Chabad of Austin) and Rabbi Shimon Lazaroff's first meetings with UT students (1972).

117732.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life & Learning
117732.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo, 'Chabad's 50-year Lone Star Journey'): after the Dubrawskys went to Dallas in 1984, 'The next year, Rabbi Chaim and Rivkie Block opened in San Antonio.' Other accounts agree the center was founded in 1985 by Rabbi Chaim and Rivkie Block and moved in 1987 to a larger site in the North Central area.

117729.name: Chabad Lubavitch
117729.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo): 'In 1986, Chabad El Paso was established with Rabbi Yisroel and Chana Greenberg appointed as directors.' CrownHeights.info (2011, 'After 25 Years, Next Generation Serves at Synagogue') and others put the Greenbergs' arrival in 1986 too.

4816645.name: Chabad Israeli Center
4816645.note: The Jewish Herald-Voice's 2022 history of Chabad in Texas (ChabadInfo): 'Houston opening its latest Chabad House in 2020 – the Israeli Center, serving Hebrew-speaking and Israeli families of Houston' (Rabbi Mendel Raichik). The chabad.org listing (4816645) is from about 2020.

6293873.name: Chabad of Lubbock at Texas Tech University
6293873.note: Lubavitch.com, 21 Nov 2024 ('Lubbock, Texas Welcomes Chabad Presence'): 'Rabbi Zalman and Chana Liba Braun moved to Lubbock earlier this year, to serve the needs of Jewish students at Texas Tech as well as the local Jewish community'; Lubbock had been 'the largest remaining U.S. city without a Chabad presence'. (Their first visits, with Chanukah menorah lightings, came before the move.)

4814414.name: Chabad of Texas Towns
4814414.note: COLlive, 16 Feb 2021 (after Chabad.org, 15 Feb 2021, 'Chabad on the Range Serving Jews in Rural Texas'): 'Rabbi Saadya and Chaya Sara Kaufmann ... have established Chabad of Texas Towns', launched during the coronavirus pandemic; 'In the fall, the Kaufmanns organized a Sukkah mobile ... and on Chanukah, they held the first-ever public menorah-lighting in Beaumont' (fall 2020). They live in Houston.

4158975.name: Chabad of Richardson and UTD
4158975.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Richardson and UTD was established in 2021' (Rabbi Shmuly and Dini Druk). The chabad.org listing (4158975) is older, about 2018-19.

6522358.name: Chabad of the Park Cities
6522358.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of the Park Cities was founded in 2024'; Rabbi Baruch and Mooka Hecht 'moved to University Park in spring 2024' to start the area's first Jewish community (he came to Dallas nearly a decade earlier as co-rabbi of The Intown Chabad).

674341.name: Chabad of Southlake
674341.note: Its own About page: 'Founded in 2008, Chabad of Southlake (Arlington) is a hub of Jewish spirituality and social activities' (Rabbi Levi and Rishi Gurevitch). The chabad.org listing (674341) is from about 2008 too.

4866998.name: Chabad of Rockwall County
4866998.note: Its own 'Meet Us' page: 'Rabbi Moishy and Chana moved to Rockwall, Texas in 2020, with their 2 daughters, Musya and Leah, to start a Chabad House' (the Kalmensons).

4174253.name: Chabad of Roundrock
4174253.note: Its own About page (Jewish Round Rock): 'We have been living in Round Rock since April of 2019' (Rabbi Mendel and Mussi Marasow); the Jewish Outlook (Shalom Austin, June 2024, 'Journey of Growth'): 'Chabad of Round Rock was formed in 2019 and is led by Rabbi Mendel and Mussi Marasow'. Two sources agree. (Its site's footer reads '© 2018-2026 Jewish Round Rock', and the chabad.org listing (4174253) is from about 2018-19.)

758578.name: Chabad of West Houston
758578.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of West Houston, Inc., began its programing with High Holiday Services and other educational programs, in rented space at the JCC of West Houston, in September of 2005' (Rabbi Dovid and Elisa Goldstein, in Houston as emissaries since 1998, first with Rabbi Traxler's Chabad Outreach).

earlier.where: rented space at the JCC of West Houston

356368.name: Chabad of Uptown
