356368.note: Jewish Herald-Voice (via CrownHeights.info): 'Rabbi Chaim and Chanie Lazaroff began serving the Houston community in 2002, establishing Chabad Uptown in February 2006.' Chabad.org (June 2008): Chabad of Uptown 'just moved into temporary quarters after outgrowing its previous home'.

1595101.name: Chabad of the Bay Area
1595101.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, May 2014, 'No Torahs on Mars Yet, but One Small Step Closer'), and The Galveston County Daily News ('Jewish center opens in League City'): Rabbi Yitzchok and Malky Schmukler came in the summer of 2012 to start Chabad of the Bay Area for the Jews of Clear Lake, Pearland and Galveston.

157731.name: Chabad at Rice University
157731.note: Its own 'Meet the Slonim Family' page: Rabbi Shmuli (Shmuel) and Nechama Slonim 'moved to Houston in May of 2016 to establish Chabad on Campus for Jewish students in Houston' (Rice, the University of Houston and the medical schools); it was at 1950 Dryden Road before the new Grinshtein center (1915 University Blvd., ground broken 2026). But the chabad.org listing (157731) is far older (about 2004), so a Chabad at Rice existed before them, perhaps the Medical Center's: medium.

5112185.name: Cheder Lubavitch of Dallas
5112185.note: COLlive, 25 May 2021: Rabbi Aharon Simon is moving to Texas 'to serve as the principal of the new Chabad Cheder' in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex; COLlive, 22 Dec 2021: 'A newly opened Chabad Cheder in Dallas, Texas ... is providing a warm, Chasidishe Chinuch to 25 children.' (Today Rabbi Moshe Naparstek is listed.)

1279173.name: The Intown Chabad
1279173.note: Chabad.org, 5 Oct 2026 ('In Dallas, Hundreds of Young Jews Fill Synagogue Over Holiday Season'): its history 'dates back to the early 2000s', with Rabbi Mendel Dubrawsky's weekly class for singles in Uptown; 'When the Drizins, Dubrawsky's daughter and son-in-law, arrived in Dallas as emissaries in 2004', they 'began providing more programming to the young professionals', 'moved there three years later, and so The Intown Chabad was born' (2007). Its charity listing says founded in 2007.

3486373.name: Chabad Jewish Center of San Marcos Texas
3486373.note: Shalom Austin (Jewish Outlook, Feb 2025, 'San Marcos Jewish Community Is Flourishing'): 'Even before Chabad of San Marcos was officially established, Rabbi Weingarten was already actively working with Jewish students at Texas State University', setting up a new Jewish student group at the students' request in 2015; 'The Rohr Chabad of San Marcos opened its doors in 2016'. The year is that first activity; the center opened in 2016.

4887459.name: Chabad of South Austin
4887459.note: Anash.org, 29 Oct 2020 ('New Shluchim to America's Fastest-Growing City'): 'America's fastest-growing city will soon be getting a new Chabad center with the appointment of Rabbi Mendel and Rikki Hertz as the new shluchim to South Austin, Texas', under Rabbi Yosef Levertov, still raising seed money. Shalom Austin (2024): by 2021 another Chabad was needed south of the river. The year is the appointment; the first programs may have come in 2021: medium.

3872731.name: Chabad Israeli Center
3872731.note: Cause IQ, from IRS data: Chabad Israeli Center San Antonio (15511 Oak Grove Drive; EIN 84-1947648), year formed 2019. An IRS record bounds it ('by'); its start not found. The chabad.org listing (3872731) is from about 2017.

5215392.name: Maayan Chai
5215392.note: Texas Jewish Post, 1 April 2010 (p. 8, on The Portal to Texas History): Maayan Chai, a nonprofit offering Jewish learning, business networking and one-on-one advice, launched by Gavin Kam with Dan (now Rabbi) Lewin, who had hosted Sinai Cafe and studied at the Mayanot yeshiva in Jerusalem. So there by April 2010; its exact start not read (the page was unavailable).

3027143.name: Chabad Young Jewish Professionals
3027143.note: The Jewish Outlook (Shalom Austin), 21 Sept 2025 ('YJP Austin Marks 10 Years with Gala Celebration'): 'Founded in 2015 by Rabbi Mendy and Rebbetzin Mussy Levertov, YJP Austin has grown into a thriving hub for Jewish adults in their 20s, 30s, and 40s.' Also the Jewish Outlook, June 2024 ('Journey of Growth'): on moving back to Austin the Levertovs first ran young-adult programs at Chabad of Austin; 'Then in 2015, they formed Chabad Young Jewish Professionals and Downtown Austin.' Two sources agree.

4994871.name: Chabad Young Families
4994871.note: Anash.org, 23 Nov 2020 ('New Shluchim to Texas's Capital City'): Rabbi Levi and Menucha Levertov (nee Raskin) 'are moving on shlichus to his hometown to start a new division of Chabad in central Austin'; 'The Levertovs will be expanding the work of Chabad of Austin by establishing a new division focused on young families and adult education' (its fundraising page: chabadyoung.raisegiving.com). The year is the appointment; its first programs may have come in 2021: medium. (Its chabad.org listing (4994871) is from about early 2021.)

6525180.name: Chabad of Downtown SA
6525180.note: Texas Public Radio, 28 Dec 2024: the first menorah in front of the Alamo 'coincides with the opening of Chabad of Downtown SA's new Jewish cultural center at 507 East Houston St., around the corner from the Alamo'; Rabbi Levi Teldon is the center's director. Its chabad.org listing (6525180) is from about mid-2024. The Teldons had been on the staff of San Antonio's main Chabad (the Chabad Center for Jewish Life and Learning, under Rabbi Chaim Block) since about 2008.

3400376.name: The Friendship Circle of Dallas
3400376.note: Dallas Doing Good, 21 Aug 2018: 'The Friendship Circle in Dallas began in 2015'; 'So in 2015, Leah and her husband Levi [Dubrawsky] started the Dallas organization.' But the Preston Hollow Advocate (26 Jan 2023): the nonprofit, an affiliate of Chabad of North Texas, 'came to Preston Hollow in 2016', and GuideStar (Friendship Circle of Dallas Inc, EIN 81-1670111) says established 2016, likely its incorporation. Sources a year apart: medium.

2581956.name: Chabad Coastal Bend
2581956.note: COLlive, 25 Aug 2017 ('Texas Shluchim Evacuate Home'), as Hurricane Harvey neared: Rabbi Naftali and Nene Schmukler, 'Shluchim of Chabad Coastal Bend in the coastal city Corpus Christi'; 'The Canadian-born rabbi, who arrived in Texas this year'. No earlier Chabad in Corpus Christi turned up (COLlive, CrownHeights.info, ChabadInfo and Lubavitch.com searched). But its chabad.org listing (2581956) and its website's About page (2615255) both carry numbers from about mid-2014, so something may have been set up before them: medium.

117730.name: Chabad Outreach of Houston
117730.note: About 1984, counted back. Chabad.org, 4 Nov 2016: Rabbi Mendy Traxler, 'the 33-year-old rabbi' (so born about 1983), 'was born in Austin but moved to Houston as an infant when his parents, Rabbi Moishe and Shoshana Traxler, started a Chabad center there, Chabad Outreach of Houston.' The Traxlers had been appointed shluchim in Austin in 1980 (Jewish Herald-Voice, 2022), and the Levertovs came to Austin in 1984 'at the invitation of the then UT rabbi, Rabbi Traxler' (Jewish Outlook, 2024), so the move was about 1984. By 2003 Rabbi Moshe Traxler was 'today the director of Chabad Outreach in Houston' (Lubavitch.com, 11 Mar 2003). No source states the year itself: medium.

658258.name: The Friendship Circle of Houston
658258.note: Its own description (Houston Friendship Circle Inc, on Benevity): 'The Friendship Circle of Houston was established in 2004 with the goal of bringing friends and smiles to children and adults with special needs'. A Buzz Magazines directory listing says founded 2003: medium. Its adult division is older: 'Back in 1999, Rabbi Dovid Goldstein ... began visiting Jewish residents at the Richmond State Supported Living Center ... The program grew and today comprises the adult division of Houston's Friendship Circle' (Chabad.org, March 2010; the Houston Chronicle, April 2010, has the same 1999 start and the first model Seder in 2000). A Friendship Circle event at Chabad of Uptown is reported in May 2008.

7440338.name: Circle Houston Inc
7440338.note: The same organization as The Friendship Circle of Houston (658258): the same directors (Rabbi Dovid and Elisa Goldstein), the same website (circlehouston.org) and the same building (10101 Fondren Road); this newer chabad.org listing (7440338, about 2025) is under its current name. The year is the Friendship Circle's (established 2004).

3394316.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Montrose
3394316.note: Brays Oaks Management District, 28 Feb 2021: 'Rabbi Lazaroff's family members have established Chabad synagogue branches in the Medical Center, Montrose, Uptown, and nine other locations in greater Houston.' So there by early 2021 (Rabbi Peretz and Mushky Lazaroff, 1644 Bonnie Brae Street); its start not found. Its own site (jewishmontrose.org) refused the fetch (403). Lead: its chabad.org listing (3394316) is from about 2016.

119660.name: Mikvah Chaya Mushka
119660.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches: the mikvah, Chabad of El Paso (Rabbi Yisrael and Chana Greenberg, there since 1986), mikvah.org, COLlive, CrownHeights.info). Lead: its chabad.org listing (119660) is from the first batch of listings, about 2000-03.

2259836.name: Hillel Academy
2259836.note: IRS: Hillel Academy Of Tarrant County (Fort Worth), ruling Oct 2014, so it existed by then. The school in Haltom City; school leader Rabbi Dov Mandel (Chabad of Fort Worth, there since 2002). Its first year is not found. Lead: its chabad.org listing (2259836) is from about 2013.

4106454.name: Chabad of Preston Hollow
4106454.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). Rabbi Levi and Leah Dubrawsky: they moved from Dallas to Denton in March 2012 to open Chabad North Texas at UNT (CrownHeights.info, 21 May 2012; Denton Record-Chronicle, Sept 2012), came back and started the Friendship Circle of Dallas in 2015, which 'came to Preston Hollow in 2016' (Preston Hollow Advocate, 2023). Lead: its chabad.org listing (4106454) is from about 2018.

118226.name: Chabad of Fort Lee
118226.note: Its own About page: 'In the summer of 1996, Rabbi Meir and Lieba Konikov came to Fort Lee with a heartfelt mission'. Rabbi Mendel and Chaya Wuensch joined in the summer of 2019.

118402.name: Chabad of the Windsors
118402.note: Its own About page ('About Chabad of the Windsors'): 'We opened in June of 2000 and are inspired by the teachings of the Lubavitcher Rebbe'. Rabbi Sholom and Aliza Leverton.

539165.name: Chabad @ TCNJ
539165.note: Lubavitch.com (from the New Jersey Jewish News), 10 May 2005 ('Chabad at the College of New Jersey in Ewing'): 'Since its launch last fall, Chabad of TCNJ has offered students a Thursday-evening class', under Rabbi Dovid Dubov, director of Chabad Lubavitch of Greater Mercer County. Today Rabbi Akiva and Zeesy Greenbaum direct it.

878203.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life - Mountain Lakes | Boonton | Denville
878203.note: Its own Welcome page: 'The Chabad Center for Jewish Life was founded in 2009 by Rabbi Levi Dubinsky and Rivky Dubinsky', serving Mountain Lakes, Boonton and Denville.

3909147.name: Chabad of Englewood
3909147.note: Its own site: 'Rabbi Shmuel and Didi Konikov moved to Englewood in the summer of 2018' to establish it. IRS (ProPublica): Chabad of Englewood Inc, exempt from Oct 2019.

4427531.name: Chabad of Hasbrouck Heights
4427531.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of Hasbrouck Heights was established in April 2019 by Rabbi Shlomie and Mushkie Segelman, together with their beautiful children.'

5803940.name: Chabad of Mendham and Chester
5803940.note: Its own site: 'Chabad of Mendham and Chester was established at the start of 2023 and is directed by Rabbi Ari and Sarah Herson.' (Its About page: 5907070.)

117998.name: Lubavitch on the Palisades
117998.note: IRS (ProPublica): Lubavitch On The Palisades, 11 Harold St, Tenafly, exempt from March 1996, so it existed by then. The Jewish Standard (CrownHeights.info, 15 Sept 2006): 'The center's current sanctuary, built nine years ago' (about 1997); The Record (CrownHeights.info, 6 July 2011): 'Seven times in the past 14 years, the center has filed applications before city boards to expand its Harold Street quarters'. Its own site's About page has a 'Celebrating 25 Years' heading, undated. When Rabbi Mordechai and Malkie Shain began is not stated.

924164.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Morganville
924164.note: Hamodia (COLlive, 6 May 2011): of Chabad of West Monmouth County's four further centers, 'Chabad of Morganville, under the direction of Rabbi Levi and Mrs. Chanale Wolosow'. So there by 2011; its start not found. Rabbi Levi Wolosow, also Chabad of Western Monmouth County's adult education director, died in Feb 2025. Lead: its chabad.org listing (924164) is from about 2009.

1110855.name: Friendship Circle of Greater Mercer County
1110855.note: IRS (ProPublica): Friendship Circle Of Greater Mercer County A Nj Nonprofit Corporation, Princeton, exempt from Dec 2012, so it existed by then; its start not found. Rabbi Shmuel Dovid and Mushky Wilhelm. Lead: its chabad.org listing (1110855) is from about 2010.

405402.name: Mei Menachem Community Mikvah
405402.note: Its own site (Chabad Center of Northwest NJ), 'Mikvah Inauguration': photos 'at the inauguration of Mikvah Mei Menachem, on Monday, July 13, 2009'; 'the first Community Mikvah established in Northwest New Jersey', in the Chabad Educational Center, which opened in the fall of 2008 and was dedicated in June 2009 (Lubavitch.com, 12 June 2009). Its chabad.org listing (405402) is from about 2006, while it was being planned.

828109.name: Hebrew High
828109.note: Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 24 Nov 2005), at the groundbreaking of the Chabad Educational Center: 'the popularity of its preschool, classes, Hebrew school and new Hebrew high have filled its cozy synagogue and ground floor classrooms'. New in the fall of 2005; whether it began that school year or the one before is not stated: medium. It moved into the new Chabad Educational Center when it opened in the fall of 2008.

earlier.where: Chabad Center of Northwest NJ, One Torah Way, Rockaway

118912.name: Chabad Early Learning Center
118912.note: The preschool of the Chabad Center of Northwest NJ (established at the start of 1988). Lubavitch.com, 24 Nov 2005: 'Preschool director Flory Heller' at the groundbreaking of the Educational Center; the Daily Record (CrownHeights.info, 15 Nov 2005): the center had become 'a synagogue, a preschool and a Hebrew school that has already outgrown its 10-year home on Torah Way'. So there by 2005; its start not stated. It moved into the Chabad Educational Center when it opened in the fall of 2008 (its About page). Lead: its chabad.org listing (118912) is from about 2002.

earlier.where: Chabad Center of Northwest NJ, One Torah Way, Rockaway

120058.name: David Hoffman Hebrew School
120058.note: The Hebrew school of the Chabad Center of Northwest NJ (established at the start of 1988; at first the Hersons held Shabbat services and 'eventually classes for children, men and women' in a VFW hall, then from about 1995 in their building on Torah Way). The Daily Record (CrownHeights.info, 15 Nov 2005): 'a Hebrew school that has already outgrown its 10-year home on Torah Way'; Lubavitch.com (24 Nov 2005): 'Hebrew School director Sarah Herson'. So there by 2005; its own start not stated. It moved into the Chabad Educational Center in the fall of 2008. Lead: its chabad.org listing (120058) is from about 2003.

earlier.where: Chabad Center of Northwest NJ, One Torah Way, Rockaway

118338.name: Chabad of Livingston
118338.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 26 Aug 2019, 'It Takes a LifeTown'): 'When the Grossbaums arrived in Livingston, in the summer of 1996 to serve as Chabad emissaries they immersed themselves in developing Jewish educational programs ... under the auspices of the Rabbinical College of America.' Rabbi Zalman and Toba Grossbaum then founded the Friendship Circle (about 2000) and LifeTown. IRS: Chabad of Livingston Inc, exempt from March 2018 (a later registration).

483891.name: Mikvah Chana
483891.note: The Star-Ledger (CrownHeights.info, 27 Feb 2007, 'Mikvah Ritual finds new Adherents'): 'Mikvah Chana, which opened in December in Livingston', in a house built on North Livingston Avenue; Rabbi Zalman Grossbaum of Chabad of Livingston quoted.

3633173.name: Chabad House Margate
3633173.note: The Margate Chabad House of Chabad of Atlantic County (Rabbi Shmuel and Tova Rapoport, sent to the Shore in 1984): its headquarters, 'based in Margate, N.J.' (Jewish Exponent, 19 July 2006). The South Jersey Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 17 June 2008), as the Ventnor shul opened: 'The Pinchus Kiedjan Chabad House in Margate will continue to be used for educational classes, JLI courses, Chabad offices and the Gan Israel Day Camp.' So there by 2006; when the Margate house began is not stated. Its own chabad.org listing (3633173) is from about 2017, after the main center moved to a former church in Ventnor (Aug 2015).

1789519.name: Cheder Menachem
1789519.note: Its own About page: 'Founded in 2004 by Rabbi D. Dubov, the Cheder grew from a small home school to its current size and location' (Rabbi Dovid Dubov, Chabad of Greater Mercer County). The NJ Jewish News (CrownHeights.info, 24 Feb 2010): 'The school was established seven years ago in the Princeton basement of Rabbi Dovid Dubov'; 'It ended up last year in rented space at Congregation B'nai Tikvah, a Conservative synagogue in North Brunswick' (1001 Finnegans Lane, where it still is). That count-back gives about 2003, against the school's own 2004, so medium.

earlier.where: Princeton, in the basement of Rabbi Dovid Dubov's home (a small home school)

118579.name: Chabad of SE Morris County
118579.note: Chabad.org, 17 July 2008 ('Civil Rights on the Docket'): the second-annual Jewish Law Symposium, 'a project of Chabad-Lubavitch of Southeast Morris County', founded by Rabbi Shalom Lubin, 'executive director of the sponsoring Chabad House'. So there by 2008; its start not found (its own site has no year). Today at 42 Park Avenue, Madison (Jewish Federation of Greater MetroWest). Lead: its chabad.org listing (118579) is from the first batch of listings, about 2002.

118626.name: Chabad of Montville Township
118626.note: IRS (ProPublica): 'Chabad Of Nothwest New Jersey Montville Township Inc', Pine Brook, exempt from Aug 2014, so it existed by then (an older start is likely); its start not found (its own site has no year). Rabbi Yosef and Chaya Schera Spalter, 325 Changebridge Road. Lead: its chabad.org listing (118626) is from the first batch of listings, about 2002.

119068.name: Hebrew School
119068.note: Chabad of Western Monmouth County's 25th-year dinner (CrownHeights.info, 5 June 2013): 'The community Chabad Hebrew School in Marlboro is directed by Rabbi Shmuly Volovick.' So there by 2013; its start not found. Lead: its chabad.org listing (119068) is from about 2003, before the Voloviks (married 2010).

119959.name: Mikvah Bais Chana
119959.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). The Morristown mikvah (Rabbinical College of America area). Lead: its chabad.org listing (119959) is from about 2003.

1420054.name: The Fair Lawn Gemach
1420054.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). A gemach of Anshei Lubavitch of Fair Lawn (fairlawnchabad.com). Lead: its chabad.org listing (1420054) is from about 2010.

5574170.name: Chabad of Fishtown @ Northern Liberties
5574170.note: Merkos 'New Shluchim' grants (COLlive, 19 Nov 2022), a two-year grant for couples in their first years: 'Rabbi and Mrs. Berel and Bracha Paltiel, Fishtown, PA'. So there by Nov 2022; its start not found. Lead: its chabad.org listing (5574170) is from about 2022.

5653140.name: Simha Maftsir Preschool
5653140.note: The Jewish Standard, 21 Nov 2018: Rabbi Mayer and Chanie Gurkov joined the Wayne-based Chabad Center of Passaic County; 'They will direct the future Chabad preschool, which is in development'. So it opened after Nov 2018 (a 2024 child-care listing names the Chabad Center of Passaic County Pre-School, 196 Ratzer Rd); its opening year not found. Lead: its chabad.org listing (5653140) is from about 2022.

6998028.name: Chabad of Linden
6998028.note: IRS (ProPublica): Chabad Of Linden Inc, Roselle Park, exempt from April 2026, so it existed by then; its start not found (its site, chabadofgl.org, has no year). Rabbi Menachem Mendel and Zissel Gurary. Lead: its chabad.org listing (6998028) is from about 2025.

7210685.name: Jewish Learning Center of Springfield
7210685.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches; its site would not resolve). Rabbi Mendy Avtzon. Lead: its chabad.org listing (7210685) is from about 2025.

7403210.name: CTeen Of Fair Lawn
7403210.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). CTeen of Anshei Lubavitch of Fair Lawn (Rabbi Levi Neubort). Lead: its chabad.org listing (7403210) is from about 2026.

7425308.name: Chabad at Drew University
7425308.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). Under Rabbi Shalom Lubin (Chabad of SE Morris County, Madison). Lead: its chabad.org listing (7425308) is from about 2026.

2751379.name: Chabad Student Center - Allentown, PA
2751379.note: CrownHeights.info, 6 Sept 2015 ('New Shluchim to Pennsylvania'): Rabbi Boruch and Rivkah Greenberg 'will be moving on Shlichus to Allentown, Pennsylvania, where they will establish a campus Chabad House at Muhlenberg College', under Chabad of Allentown (Rabbi Yaacov and Deborah Halperin).

1618146.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Yardley
1618146.note: Jewish Exponent, 30 Aug 2023: 'Rabbi Zalman Blecher and Rebbetzin Chaya Blecher arrived in Yardley in the secular year of 2015'; 'So that's what we've been doing since 2015 as an affiliate of the Lubavitch of Bucks County'; it rents space on Yardley Newtown Road. But its chabad.org listing (1618146) and The Shul at Yardley's (1618143) are both from about 2011, so Lubavitch of Bucks County may have had something in Yardley before them: medium.

1618143.name: The Shul at Yardley
1618143.note: The shul of the Lubavitch of Yardley (Rabbi Zalman Blecher, who came in 2015; the Jewish Exponent, 2023: after they moved they 'had trouble attracting a minyan to Shabbat services'). Its chabad.org listing (1618143) is from about 2011, like Chabad Lubavitch of Yardley's: medium.

117722.name: Chabad of Scranton
117722.note: CrownHeights.info, 24 June 2008: 'Harav Leibel Itkin a Shliach in Scranton, PA'; COLlive, 10 Dec 2008: a Mumbai memorial in Scranton 'organized by Shliach Laibel Itkin'. So there by 2008; its start not found. Rabbi Yehuda (Leibel) Itkin was also a contract chaplain at SCI Waymart from 1993 (Pennsylvania Dept. of Corrections, 2023) and is senior rabbi of Ohav Zedek in Scranton. Lead: its chabad.org listing (117722) is from the first batch of listings, about 2000-03.

117714.name: Bais Menachem Youth Development Program
117714.note: Ami Magazine, 24 May 2017 ('Revitalization by the River'): 'His son, Rabbi Uri Perlman, founded a yeshivah for boys in need of an alternative educational environment, in 1999'; its first rebbeim formed the nucleus of Kingston's Chabad community. Anash.org (27 July 2020): 'The first anash families began moving in when his son, Rabbi Uri Perlman, opened the Bais Menachem yeshiva twenty years ago.' Rabbi Zvi Perlman, the first Lubavitcher there, came as a rebbe at the Hebrew day school in 1977.

117607.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Georgia
117607.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007, 'The Rebbe's Minyan'): 'When Rabbi New arrived in what is now the city of Sandy Springs in 1984 ... he set up the only Chabad center in Georgia, dubbed Chabad of Georgia'; also 'since Rabbi Yossi New arrived 23 years ago in an area where Chabad had failed to establish a foothold more than a decade earlier'. Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): 'It's been 30 years since Rabbi Yossi and Dassie New first arrived in Atlanta'; '"It was 1984 ..."'. Its synagogue is Congregation Beth Tefillah, Sandy Springs.

118230.name: Chabad Intown
118230.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'Rabbi Schusterman, who established the center in 1997 and still leads it'; 'the center began on the second floor of Congregation Anshi S'fard in Virginia-Highland after he set up Chabad on Campus'; 'Chabad found a larger space in April 2000 on Ponce de Leon Avenue'. Today at 730 Ponce De Leon Place NE (whether that is the 2000 building is not stated). Rabbi Eliyahu and Dena Schusterman.

earlier.where: second floor of Congregation Anshi S'fard, Virginia-Highland

118608.name: Chabad at Emory
118608.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'Rabbi Eliyahu Schusterman, who heads Chabad Intown, started the campus branch on a part-time basis in 1997. When it went full time in 2000, Chabad barely had enough students for Rosh Hashanah services' (Rabbi Zalman Lipskier, its director since).

118208.name: Chabad of Augusta
118208.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 Nov 2022: 'In 1996, the first Chabad center was established by Rabbi Zalman and Chani Fischer, to serve the needs of the Jewish community. Fast forward 26 years'. Agreeing: the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): 'Augusta has had a Chabad center for more than a decade. Going into his 12th year as the full-time founding rabbi, Zalman Fisher'. In 2022 Rabbi Mendel and Sarah Fischer joined.

531722.name: Chabad Israeli Center
531722.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'The Chabad Israeli Center recently opened in Sandy Springs. Lead by Rabbi New's son-in-law, Rabbi Mendy Gurary'. Today at 4276 Chamblee Dunwoody Road.

earlier.where: Sandy Springs (where it opened)

307665.name: Chabad of Athens-UGA
307665.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): Rabbi Michoel Refson: 'The first week we hosted Shabbat dinner when we arrived in 2005, we had four students around the table'. Agreeing: Chabad.org, 1 May 2008: the 'three-year-old' Chabad House; 'When they arrived to the school three years ago'. Its own center (279 Meigs Street) was due to open in fall 2008.

6500282.name: CMCH Elementary
6500282.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): Rabbi Isser New 'in 2010, the year the first- through sixth-grade Montessori-style elementary school first started'; 'it is now starting its fifth year, with 52 students'. The Chaya Mushka Children's House elementary school of Chabad of Georgia. Its chabad.org listing (6500282) is a new one, from about 2024.

527027.name: Kennesaw Chabad Jewish Center
527027.note: Began as the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth. CrownHeights.info, 4 Feb 2008: Rabbi Zalman and Nechami Charytan 'have recently moved on Shlichus to Acworth, GA where they have established the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth serving the Jewish residents of North West Cobb County'; Chabad.org, 23 Nov 2008: the Charytans 'established the Chabad-Lubavitch Jewish Center of Acworth, Ga., this year'. But the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007) said they would arrive 'in November' 2007, so they may have moved in late 2007: medium. Today at 3590 Frey Lake Road NW, Kennesaw (when it moved is not stated).

earlier.where: Acworth (the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth)

117893.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Cobb County
117893.note: About 1991. The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Ephraim Silverman, 'Since landing in Cobb County in 1999, eight years after Chabad opened there'. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution (CrownHeights.info, 26 Jan 2006): 'The congregation of Chabad of Cobb started with only a few families in the early 1990s. They met regularly to worship in a rented classroom and later in a storefront of a converted bakery in an east Cobb shopping center. In 1995, they bought a 40-year-old house on Lower Roswell Road'; Silverman director since 2000. That house was torn down in 2006 for the new building (4450 Lower Roswell Road, finished about 2008); meanwhile it rented space in a shopping center on Johnson Ferry Road (AJT, 2007). The year is worked out, not stated: medium.

earlier.where: a rented classroom
a storefront (a converted bakery) in an east Cobb shopping center
rented space in a shopping center on Johnson Ferry Road (while its Lower Roswell Road building was rebuilt)

118282.name: Chabad of North Fulton
118282.note: Its own page: 'Chabad of North Fulton was established in 1998 to serve as a center for Jewish life and education in North Fulton County'; 'From 1998-2008 we operated under the name "Chabad of Alpharetta"', renamed in January 2009 after Johns Creek and Milton were incorporated. The Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Hirshy Minkowicz 'is entering his ninth year along the new border between Alpharetta and Johns Creek'.

118517.name: The Chabad Enrichment Center of Gwinnett
118517.note: Its own About page: 'Since opening our doors in 2001, we have become the center for Jewish connection for hundreds of families.' Agreeing: the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Yossi and Esther Lerman 'are entering their seventh year in Gwinnett'. In 2007 they bought land at Spalding and Crooked Creek drives in Norcross; today at 6251 Smithpoint Drive, Peachtree Corners.

4068219.name: Chabad Decatur
4068219.note: COLlive, 14 Aug 2018 ('New Shluchim to Decatur, GA'): Rabbi Avremi and Bracha Slavaticki (nee Nemes) 'have recently moved to Decatur, Georgia, to establish the city's first Chabad Center'.

4614681.name: Chabad of Rural Georgia
4614681.note: COLlive, 29 Jan 2020 ('New Shluchim to Rural Georgia'): Rabbi Chaim and Chaya Markovits (nee Mentz) 'have recently been appointed as the new Shluchim to Rural Georgia', for Jews distant from established Jewish communities.

5540093.name: Chabad of Downtown Roswell
5540093.note: COLlive, 21 March 2022 ('New Shluchim to Roswell, Georgia'): Rabbi Chaim and Menucha Schwartz 'have been appointed as the Shluchim to Roswell, Georgia, where they will establish a new Chabad house'; he grew up in Roswell.

5540514.name: Chabad of Dunwoody
5540514.note: COLlive, 31 July 2022 ('New Shluchim to Dunwoody, Georgia'): Rabbi Mendy and Sara Wineberg (nee Thaler) 'will be moving on Shlichus to Dunwoody' and 'will be establishing Chabad of Dunwoody'; 'this will be the first Chabad Center in the area'.

3336359.name: Chabad of Forsyth
3336359.note: Forsyth County News (CrownHeights.info, 26 Oct 2016): Chabad-Lubavitch 'opened up a location in March on Peachtree Parkway in Cumming' (Rabbi Levi Mentz). Its new center south of Cumming, the first synagogue in Forsyth County, opened at the end of May 2017 (Forsyth County News / CrownHeights.info, 5 June 2017; Atlanta Jewish Times, Aug 2017). Today at 795 Brannon Road, Cumming.

earlier.where: Peachtree Parkway, Cumming

3971058.name: Chabad of Toco Hills
3971058.note: About 2016, counted back. Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 11 Feb 2026): 'Chabad of Toco Hills was established ten years ago by Rabbi Yale and Rickelle New'; in the early years services were held in homes, classes 'wherever space was available', and the local school's classrooms or gym were rented for larger events; its president since 2017; now a new $3 million center. No source states the year itself: medium. Its chabad.org listing (3971058) is from about 2017.

earlier.where: homes and rented school classrooms in Toco Hills (no fixed address)

1788196.name: Chabad of Peachtree City
1788196.note: Its own About page: 'Chabad of Peachtree City, on Atlanta's Southside, was established in 2011 by Rabbi Yossi and Shternie Lew' (emissaries in Atlanta since 1993). But they moved to Peachtree City only in 2012: The Citizen (14 Aug 2012): 'Chabad House of Peachtree City became a reality earlier this month' when the Lews bought their home at 219 Kelvington Way, programs to start in about three weeks; the Atlanta Jewish Times (23 Oct 2015): 'The Lews moved to Peachtree City in 2012 just before Rosh Hashanah', served the south side 'for several years from their home', and planned to move within weeks into a new building on 2.5 acres in Tyrone (632 Dogwood Trail). A year apart: medium.

earlier.where: the Lews' home, 219 Kelvington Way, Peachtree City

1610198.name: Rohr Chabad House at Georgia Tech and Georgia State
1610198.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 2 Jan 2012): 'This past fall, Chabad of Downtown Universities, which serves students from GSU and the Georgia Institute of Technology, officially opened its doors, with Rabbi Shlomo and Shifra Sharfstein as its directors' (before that, Emory's Rabbi Zalman Lipskier and Rabbi Shlomo Elkan ran programs at GSU). Agreeing: the Atlanta Jewish Times (24 Aug 2015): 'The couple moved to Atlanta from New York four years ago'; 'They started out using a small house several blocks away'; the Rohr Chabad House at 471 10th St. in Midtown opened on Sunday, 30 Aug 2015.

earlier.where: a small house several blocks from 471 10th St., Midtown

1667008.name: Friendship Circle of Atlanta
1667008.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 27 Aug 2015): 'Rabbi Yale and Rickelle New began Friendship Circle of Atlanta in December 2011, soon after the couple married. From their home in the Toco Hills neighborhood'. Today directed by Rabbi Shlomo and Chanky Freedman.

earlier.where: the News' home in Toco Hills

5274556.name: Chabad of Hall County
5274556.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times, 1 Sept 2022 ('Hall County has a New Jewish Center'): 'Chabad of Hall, founded in February 2022 by Rabbi Nechemia and Shaina Gurevitz'.

5541057.name: CTeen of Atlanta
5541057.note: Lubavitch.com, 28 Aug 2022 ('Trailblazing Former CTeener to Open Innovative Atlanta CTeen Center'): Rabbi Dovid and Talya Goldshmidt 'are now opening CTeen of Atlanta', a stand-alone teen center.

542450.name: Intown Jewish Preschool
542450.note: About 2007, counted back. CrownHeights.info, 14 Dec 2011: 'the Intown Jewish Preschool, which has grown rapidly over the 4 years – from 7 children to 45 children'; its own About page: it began as a 'Mother's Morning Out' with seven children in its current building, the former Canterbury Preschool (604 Cooledge Avenue NE), after the founders saw the need 'In the early 2000's'. The Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007) said a $500,000 matching grant 'will help Chabad launch the Intown Jewish Preschool', so it may have opened in 2008: medium. Dena Schusterman, founding director.

4752247.name: Chabad of Smyrna
4752247.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times, 10 Aug 2023 ('Chabad of Smyrna-Vinings Reaches Out'): Rabbi Avremel and Mushky Zaltzman 'hosted the first public Chanukah menorah lighting for the area in December 2019 at Taylor-Brawner Park'; their start is not stated. So there by Dec 2019. Lead: its chabad.org listing (4752247) is from about 2020.

3698295.name: Chabad of Savannah
3698295.note: Chabad.org obituary of Rabbi Yehuda Refson (CrownHeights.info, 24 March 2020) lists his son 'Rabbi Zalman Refson (Savannah, Ga.)'. So there by March 2020; its start not found (its own site gives no year). Lead: its chabad.org listing (3698295) is from about 2017.

4858926.name: Chabad Buckhead & Brookhaven
4858926.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times, 1 Oct 2025 ('Young Rabbi Inspires Buckhead Condo Circuit'): Rabbi Yisrael New's 'three-year-old Chabad center The Buckhead Shul' (so about 2022), on East Wesley, 'after exiting a smaller space on Pharr Road'. Its chabad.org listing (4858926) is from about 2020-21, so the center may be older than the shul: only a bound.

earlier.where: a smaller space on Pharr Road, Buckhead

5867802.name: The Torah Center ATL
5867802.note: JF&CS Atlanta event listing (Jan 2025): 'This past year, Rabbi Sollish became the Director and Instructor at The Torah Center Atlanta' (Rabbi Ari Sollish, founder of the Intown Jewish Academy). So there by 2024; its start not found. Lead: its chabad.org listing (5867802) is from about 2023.

117649.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life
117649.note: The News & Observer (CrownHeights.info, 12 Dec 2008): 'The first Chabad House in the Tar Heel state was started in 1980 by Rabbi Yossi Groner of Charlotte.' Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 29 March 2025): 'Chabad in Charlotte was founded by Mushka's grandparents, Rabbi Yossi and Mariashi Groner, in 1980'. Rabbi Groner's own account (JEM, interviewed 2013; Anash.org, 9 Oct 2025): head emissary to North and South Carolina 'since 1980'; other biographies: sent 'in the summer of 1980'.

117650.name: Jewish Life Center - Chabad of Raleigh - Cong. Sha'arei Israel
117650.note: Chabad.org: Rabbi Pinchas Herman, 'who, along with his wife Helena and three children, started the Chabad center in 1989 in this community of about 5,000 Jews', rabbi of Sha'arei Israel. Agreeing: Rabbi Yossi Groner (JEM, interviewed 2013; Anash.org, 9 Oct 2025): in 1988 the committee of Raleigh's Congregation Shaarei Israel decided to partner with Chabad; 'Shaarei Israel ultimately merged with Chabad, and Rabbi Pinny Herman moved to Raleigh'. Sha'arei Israel itself began in 1979 as Raleigh's only Orthodox synagogue.

117724.name: Chabad of South Carolina
117724.note: The State (CrownHeights.info, 17 June 2012): 'Hesh Epstein first came to Columbia in the late 1980s, along with his childhood friend Rabbi Meir Muller, as part of an Chabad outreach mission' (the officiant's father had married Hesh and Chavi Epstein 27 years earlier, about 1985). So it began in the late 1980s; the year itself not found. (The Jewish Historical Society of SC's 'opened its doors to the public in 2015' is a later building, Chabad Aleph House.)

117725.name: Chabad of Myrtle Beach
117725.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 3 Feb 2014): 'The Aizenmans moved to Myrtle Beach in 1987 from Brooklyn.' Chabadpedia: Rabbi Doron Aizenman, shliach in Myrtle Beach 'since 1987'. The Charlotte Jewish News (May 1988) reported the dedication of the Chabad House in Myrtle Beach on 13 March 1988.

118525.name: Chabad of Durham / Chapel Hill
118525.note: Chabad.org, 21 Jan 2013 ('A Home Away from Home for Duke U. Patients'): Rabbi Zalman and Yehudis Bluming 'moved to town in 2002 as co-directors of Chabad-Lubavitch serving Duke University'. Another Chabad.org piece: they 'established Chabad in the Durham/Chapel Hill region in 2002'. Today at 127 Mallette Street, Chapel Hill.

119657.name: Cutler Jewish Day School
119657.note: Private School Review: 'Year Founded 1992'. Rabbi Meir Muller is described as its co-founder, who 'spent 30 years heading the school' (BJELA biography). IRS ruling 2001. A directory year, not confirmed by a dated report: medium.

392029.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Western North Carolina
392029.note: Asheville Citizen-Times (CrownHeights.info, 21 Sept 2006, 'First full-time Chabad rabbi comes to Asheville'): Rabbi Shaya and Chana Susskind 'have moved to Asheville in order to establish Chabad Lubavitch of Western North Carolina'.

506593.name: Chabad of Charleston & The Low Country
506593.note: About 2007, counted back. Mount Pleasant Magazine, 10 Dec 2015: Rabbi Yossi Refson 'arrived in the Charleston area with his wife, Sarah, and 3-and-a-half-year-old son from New York eight years ago and established Chabad of Charleston and the Lowcountry'; its Center for Jewish Life on Mathis Ferry Road was due to open in May 2016 (College of Charleston's Mapping Jewish Charleston: opened 2016). Before that the Refsons hosted Shabbat dinners and classes at their home. Its chabad.org listing (506593) is from about 2007.

earlier.where: the Refsons' home, Mount Pleasant

558872.name: Chabad of Wilmington
558872.note: About 2007, counted back. Chabad.org via JNS (Heritage Florida Jewish News, 21 Sept 2018): 'For the last 11 years, the Lieblich family of Wilmington, N.C., have always held Rosh Hashanah services on both days of the holiday' (Rabbi Moshe and Chana Lieblich, co-directors). The News & Observer (12 Dec 2008) lists a Chabad house in Wilmington; its chabad.org listing (558872) is from about 2007. No source states the year itself: medium.

661035.name: Ballantyne Jewish Center
661035.note: South Charlotte News (CrownHeights.info, 24 Aug 2012): Rabbi Yisroel and Leah (nee Groner) Levin started the Ballantyne Jewish Center; 'Starting in 2008, they first ran the center out of their home'. Today at 8632 Bryant Farms Road.

earlier.where: the Levins' home, Ballantyne

699445.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Greensboro
699445.note: CrownHeights.info, 8 July 2008 ('New Shluchim to North Carolina'): Rabbi Yosef and Hindy (nee Zaklos) Plotkin 'will IYH be moving on Shlichus to Greensboro, North Carolina, where they will establish a new Chabad House'.

1680993.name: Chabad of Greenville
1680993.note: COLlive, 13 May 2012 ('New Shluchim to Carolina's Upstate'): Rabbi Leibel and Musie (nee Posner) Kesselman 'are moving to Greenville, South Carolina on Shlichus'. Today at 3515 E North Street.

2753679.name: Chabad @ the University of South Carolina
2753679.note: Its own page ('Who are we'): 'Rabbi and Mrs. Epstein moved to South Carolina in early 2015 to open a Chabad House' for students at the University of South Carolina (Rabbi Sruly and Shlomit Epstein). Today at 1531 Washington Street.

3109644.name: Chabad at Elon University
3109644.note: Elon News Network (Oct 2017): 'until December 2015, Elon was not one of them'; Rabbi Mendy and Rivka Minkowitz run it from their home on Truitt Drive (still its address, 107 Truitt Drive).

3932955.name: Chabad of Lake Norman
3932955.note: Lubavitch.com, 30 Oct 2018: 'In late September, as Hurricane Florence made landfall, Rabbi Chaim and Chaya Greenberg and their baby, Rivka, opened the doors of Chabad of Lake Norman.'

4026366.name: Chabad Young Professionals Raleigh
4026366.note: Rabbi Zalmy and Mushka Dubinsky moved to downtown Raleigh in 2018 to open CYP (Anash.org; Chabad.org via CrownHeights.info, 20 Sept 2024; Raleigh Magazine, Sept 2025: founded about seven years earlier). It outgrew their home and moved into the former Young Hearts Distilling building downtown (225 S Wilmington St), announced Sept 2024, opened as The Shul Downtown in January 2025.

earlier.where: the Dubinskys' home, downtown Raleigh

4399500.name: Chabad Serving Wake Forest University & Winston Salem
4399500.note: COLlive, 11 Aug 2019 ('New Shluchim to North Carolina'): Rabbi Levi and Shaina Gurevitz (nee Rapoport) 'are moving on Shlichus to Winston Salem, North Carolina to service Jewish students and the local Jews', including Wake Forest University.

5582467.name: ZABS Place
5582467.note: Founded by Bentzion and Rochel Groner and Charlie and Caren Gale, it 'opened in November 2014' (its own site; WSOC-TV marked its fifth year in 2019). A thrift boutique and job-training center for young adults with special needs, a division of Chabad of Charlotte, at 100 North Trade Street, Matthews.

6054501.name: Chabad of NC State University
6054501.note: Anash.org, 6 Nov 2023 ('New Shliach Will Serve as First Mohel in the Carolinas'): Rabbi Shmuly and Chaya Sara (nee Heber) Meijers 'have recently moved on shlichus to Raleigh, North Carolina' to serve students at North Carolina State University.

6782748.name: Chabad Israeli Center of Charlotte
6782748.note: Anash.org, 19 March 2025: Rabbi Sholom Ber and Mushka Pevzner joined Chabad of Charlotte to serve the Hebrew-speaking community and 'have already made a strong impact in Charlotte by hosting a Seder, Chanukah mivtzoim, and a Tu Bishvat gathering' (so a Seder in spring 2024); Chabad.org (29 March 2025): they 'have recently moved to Charlotte'. Worked out from the events: medium.

334145.name: Chabad of Cary Jewish Center
334145.note: About 2005, counted back. Shalom Raleigh, 10 Jan 2025: about 20 years earlier Rabbi Aaron and Leah Herman began coming to Cary from Raleigh to lead services and classes, which planted the seeds of Chabad of Cary; Rabbi Yisroel Cotlar moved to Cary in 2010 as its first full-time rabbi. The News & Observer (12 Dec 2008) already lists a Chabad house in Cary; its chabad.org listing (334145) is from about 2005. Medium.

5585894.name: Chabad Torah Academy
5585894.note: Anash.org, 9 March 2023 ('New Lubavitcher Cheder Blossoms in North Carolina'): the new Chabad Cheder of North Carolina, founded by the shluchim of central North Carolina under Rabbi Yossi Groner, 'began with the youngest grades, starting with only 5 children' and now has 25 through second grade; Rabbi Gavi and Mushky Schwei were brought in to head it. So there by early 2023; its first year not stated. Lead: its chabad.org listing (5585894) is from about 2022.

3201321.name: The Uptown Chabad
3201321.note: The Charlotte Jewish News (April 2016) lists a young professionals' Seder led by Rabbi Motti and Chaya Groner at Chabad of Uptown, 410 North Smith Street, Suite IB (seen through a search result; DigitalNC could not be opened from here). So there by spring 2016; its start not found. IRS ruling 2022. Lead: its chabad.org listing (3201321) is from about 2015-16.

4090936.name: Chabad of Greater Hilton Head
4090936.note: Jewish Historical Society of South Carolina: 'Started in the mid-2010s, Bluffton's Chabad', founded by Rabbi Mendel and Sheina Hertz; its address there, 83 Kenwood Dr., Bluffton, differs from today's (395 Hampton Pkwy, Bluffton). Only 'the mid-2010s' is known. Lead: its chabad.org listing (4090936) is from about 2018.

earlier.where: 83 Kenwood Dr., Bluffton

7401983.name: Cteen Raleigh
7401983.note: No dated source found yet (Nov 2026 searches). CTeen of Chabad of Raleigh (Rabbi Mendy Wilschanski), 7400 Falls of Neuse Rd. Lead: its chabad.org listing (7401983) is from about 2026.

117716.name: Lubavitch House of Philadelphia
117716.note: Rabbi Menachem Schmidt's Lubavitch House; this listing is its office (754 S 9th St, in the Italian Market area), and the Vilna Congregation (119651) is its department. Philadelphia City Paper (CrownHeights.info, 27 Aug 2009): Schmidt 'has spearheaded various Lubavitch operations in Philadelphia since 1980'; he and his wife opened the Lubavitch House at Penn in 1980 (listing 117945: the Daily Pennsylvanian, JNS). Chabad.org (19 May 2008): 'From a cluttered and cramped office in the Italian Market area of South Philadelphia – he moved there in 1990 –' Schmidt runs the Jewish Business Network, Jewish Relief Agency and Jewish Heritage Programs and 'retains his position as executive director of the Lubavitch House'.

earlier.where: University City, at the Lubavitch House at Penn (4032 Spruce St), where it began; the office moved to the Italian Market area in 1990 (the Penn house is still its campus Chabad House, listing 117945)

119651.name: Chabad at Vilna Congregation
119651.note: The Vilna Congregation, 509 Pine St (formed in 1904 by Lithuanian immigrants; in this building since 1922). Wikipedia: 'Rabbi Menachem Schmidt was appointed in 1989' (no citation). Lubavitch.com (18 Feb 2019), citing a 1990 Jewish Exponent article: the congregation dwindled in the 80s and 'the community turned to Rabbi Schmidt'; a congregant told the Exponent, 'Without him, we'd have no synagogue ... He gave the shul new life.' So Chabad was there by 1990; the year 1989 has one source.

516456.name: The Friendship Circle, Philadelphia Region South
516456.note: Philly Friendship Circle (Rabbi Zev and Chani Baram). The Jewish Exponent (26 Oct 2022): it 'has grown from one friend to about 300 since 2004'; Zev Baram wanted to start it 'after moving to the city in 2003' and did so 'a year later'. Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 9 March 2008) agrees: a child 'has been enjoying weekly visits from Friendship Circle's teen volunteers since the program began four years ago'; 'Started with a handful of participants by Rabbi Zev and Chani Baram, leaders of Chabad of Old City Philadelphia' (then 'a project of Guideline Services-Lubavitch House'). IRS: Friendship Circle Philadelphia Region Inc (Bala Cynwyd), ruling July 2010.

6166219.name: Cheder Chabad of Philadelphia
6166219.note: COLlive and Anash (8 June 2025): 'For over 22 years, Cheder Chabad has been the beating heart of the Chabad community here'; 'What began in the basement of a local shliach's home has grown into a full, thriving school' (270 children, preschool to 8th grade); so it began by 2003. In Jan 2011 'Cheder Chabad of Greater Philadelphia' joined the 3rd annual Kinus HaChadorim (CrownHeights.info, 18 Jan 2011). In June 2025 it raised funds for a permanent home for its preschool and girls' division; its site now gives 7613 Old York Rd, Melrose Park, the CSF directory 276 S. Bryn Mawr Ave, Bryn Mawr, and the IRS 7030 Brentwood Rd, Philadelphia (none dated). IRS: Cheder Chabad - Philadelphia (EIN 27-0854753), ruling June 2014. Rabbi Mendy Levin, head of school.

earlier.where: the basement of a local shliach's home, where it began (whose not stated)

347784.name: Lubavitch of Central Bucks County West
347784.note: Chabad of Doylestown (300 E Swamp Rd). The Jewish Exponent (27 June 2025): 'Rabbi Mendel Prus has been the head of the Chabad of Doylestown for a little less than 20 years'; 'We really started from scratch'; their first Rosh Hashanah drew 35 people; about a decade ago it ran a campaign for a new facility. So it began after mid-2005 (about 2006). IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Of Doylestown Inc (300 E Swamp Rd), ruling May 2015.

2929389.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Doylestown
2929389.note: The same Chabad of Doylestown (Rabbi Mendel Prus; website jewishdoylestown.com); this listing has its Jewish Community Center at 455 East Street. IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Of Doylestown Inc, ruling May 2015. The Jewish Exponent (27 June 2025) has Prus heading it 'for a little less than 20 years' (see 347784). When the East Street center opened is not found.

3408190.name: Chabad of Lewisburg
3408190.note: IRS: Chabad Of Lewisburg Inc (1 Buffalo Rd), ruling May 2017, so it existed by then. Campus Chabad House (Bucknell); Rabbi Yisroel and Mariasha Baumgarten. Its own website gives 36 South 8th Street, chabad.org and the IRS 1 Buffalo Road (undated). Its start is not found.

6010288.name: Chabad of Back Mountain
6010288.note: IRS: Chabad Of Back Mountain (Shavertown), ruling June 2024, so it existed by then. Rabbi Shlomie Sirota. Its start is not found.

1773417.name: Chabad Israeli Center
1773417.note: IRS: Chabad Israeli Center Inc (3530 Buck Rd, Huntingdon Valley), ruling Dec 2013, so it existed by then; chabad.org now gives 2755 Philmont Avenue. Rabbi Levy Weber. Its undated Hebrew About page says 'Ten years ago, Rabbi Yitzchak Weber joined Rabbi Lipskar' (no date, so not used). Its start is not found.

6162604.name: Jewish Care On Call
6162604.note: IRS: Jewish Care On Call (Philadelphia), ruling April 2022, so it existed by then. Its start is not found.

117718.name: Va'adah L'dovrei Ivrit Chabad
117718.note: Rabbi Zalman Lipsker's Israeli center (110 S 8th St). Lubavitch.com (23 Sept 2009) calls him 'Director of the Va'adah L'dovrei Ivrit Chabad – Israeli center in Philadelphia', so it existed by 2009. Anash (28 Jan 2025): Rabbi Shneur Zalman and Feiga Lipsker's shlichus in Philadelphia 'began in 1964', at first as teachers in the school, joining Rabbi Avraham Shemtov. When the Israeli center itself began is not found.

118618.name: Chabad Living Legacy
118618.note: IRS: Chabad Lubavitch Jewish Center Of Delaware County, at the listing's address (444 E Township Line Rd, Havertown), ruling July 2005, so it existed by then. Chabad.org (24 Jan 2019): 'Rabbi Eli and Rivkah Strasberg, co-direct the Chabad "Living Legacy" program'. Its start is not found.

4555491.name: Chabad of Aston
4555491.note: Chadds Ford Live (20 May 2024): 'Rabbi Yudi Gerber, of Chabad of Aston' said 'his group has been involved with the food distribution program for more than two years', so by 2022. Lead: a 2020 Delaware County Daily Times piece (behind PressReader, not read) is described as saying the Gerbers had recently founded it.

372781.name: Chabad Jewish Center
372781.note: Chabad of Abington (515 Meetinghouse Rd, Rydal; Rabbi Zushe Gurevitz). The Philadelphia Inquirer (25 March 2013), on Lubavitch of Montgomery County: 'Rabbi Deitsch also supervises groups in Rydal and Chestnut Hill.' So a Chabad group met in Rydal by 2013; when this center began, and when the Gurevitzes came, is not found.

2734156.name: Ohev Zedek - Chabad
2734156.note: Ohev Zedek, 1432 Mulberry St, Scranton. The Pennsylvania Department of Corrections (2023) gives Rabbi Yehuda (Leibel) Itkin, Chabad of Scranton's rabbi, as senior rabbi of Ohav Zedek Synagogue in Scranton, so it was a Chabad-led shul by then. When it became one is not found.

2052403.name: Chabad Jewish Learning Center
2052403.note: Rabbi Mendy Pewzner, at 3515 Green St (the address of Chabad-Lubavitch of Harrisburg, 117713). Its website (chabadjlc.org) did not answer (503); no dated source found.

155891.name: Lubavitch of Northwest Philadelphia
155891.note: Rabbi Yitzchok and Pessy Gurevitz, 7334 Rural Lane, West Mt. Airy (its site chabadnwp.org, which in Oct 2026 asks people to call for its new Shabbat location). No dated source for its start found.

5399392.name: Chabad of Pocono Pines
5399392.note: A summer and holiday center (its site says it is 'operational during the summer season and Jewish holidays'); Rabbi Nison Deitsch. No dated source found.

7375651.name: Chabad of Rural Western Pennsylvania
7375651.note: Rabbi Yisroel Gordon; a new chabad.org listing with no address. No dated source found.
